PSA: Check Your Happy Dragon Orders – Hidden Charges and Mispriced Items

I’ve been a loyal customer of Happy Dragon for several years now, frequently placing orders over $30+. Recently, I decided to question an overcharge I noticed—because this has been happening to me every time I’ve placed an order by phone. My total from the Happy Dragon Restaurant pamphlet came out to be $34.25, but I was charged $35.25. When I asked about the extra $1, I was told by the rude lady it was a “delivery fee.”

I’ve been using their most recent July 2025 menu pamphlet, which replaced the older version a few months ago. Nowhere on this updated menu is a $1 delivery fee mentioned—only a $15 minimum for delivery is clearly listed. After looking further into the charges, I discovered that they automatically include a can of soda with every order—even when I didn’t ask for one—and quietly add a $1 charge for it.

The pamphlet also makes no mention of a free soda with a minimum order, further confirming that the soda is not complimentary but is instead being charged to the customer without consent.

When my food was delivered, I asked the friendly delivery driver if there was a $1 delivery charge or soda fee. He seemed confused, said he wasn’t aware of such a charge, and advised me to ask the restaurant directly. That raised further concerns—even the delivery staff aren’t aware of what customers are being billed for.

There was also a separate instances where I ordered only Chicken with Broccoli and white rice which is priced at $11.50 under the “Chicken” section of the menu pamphlet or only Beef with Broccoli and white rice which is priced at $11.75 under the “Beef” section of the menu pamphlet. Instead, I was charged for both orders under the “Combination Platters” section priced at $13.50 each, which includes pork fried rice and an egg roll—neither of which were included in my order upon delivery. This caused me to be overcharged for an incomplete combo meal I never ordered to begin with, and it’s happened more than once.

While these may seem like small charges, they’re being added without my knowledge or approval—and this has happened every time I’ve placed a phone order over several months, which suggests a clear, intentional pattern. Formal complaints have been filed with the NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) & NYC 311. I hope Happy Dragon Chinese Restaurant takes responsibility and improves transparency in their pricing practices.

This is a PSA for all current and new customers placing phone orders: Always double-check your total and request a breakdown of charges, ensuring it matches what’s on their menu pamphlet (which is included on every delivery order). These unlisted fees and misclassifications are misleading and unfair to all Happy Dragon Chinese Restaurant customers.

I’ve been going to this pizzeria since I moved here 11 years ago, and for most of that time, I genuinely loved it. The old family who owned it provided great service, were friendly, and the pizza was always amazing.

Unfortunately, since the business was sold, my experience has been completely different. From the moment we walked in, the new owner just wasn’t friendly. I smiled and tried to greet him when we first came in, and he barely acknowledged us and just had a straight face. I understand that everyone has their own personality, but as a customer, you expect at least a little friendliness and basic customer service.

I ordered four pizzas, and honestly, they were extremely oily and pretty mediocre, especially considering how expensive they are. I also ended up getting a huge stomach ache afterward, which made the experience even worse.

The part that really bothered me, though, was what happened with the tables. This happened twice during our visit. The first time, I sat in a chair closer to the bathroom because I was waiting for it to become available. I didn’t want to keep walking back and forth from our table, and the restaurant wasn’t even busy. While I was sitting there, he came over and started wiping down the table even though it wasn’t dirty and I was still sitting there.

Then, later, my boyfriend and I were sitting at our actual table talking. We were getting ready to leave, and I was only waiting because I wanted to use the bathroom before we left, but it was still occupied. While we were still sitting there and having a conversation, he came over AGAIN and started wiping down our table while we were right there. The table wasn’t dirty, and we weren’t done yet. After that, we decided to just leave instead of waiting around.

I’ve been coming here for 11 years, so it honestly makes me sad to have such a different experience now. review_text:
An incredible Jesuit University in the Bronx.

First I'd like to address the negative reviews. It is a secure campus so no you can't take a walk on the closed secure campus just because you feel like it. Imagine the arrogance of people to leave a negative review of an incredible historic university just because they were told NO.
Then there are the handful of haters who didn't get their fannys patted whole they were students or others who got rejected.. boo hoo.

Now onto the review. Fordham is an incredible university with a global reach.
My wife is an alum and we are on campus all the time and are very involved with the school.
First the physical campus is amazing. Rose Hill is sprawling and beautiful with a ton of green space and mature trees and plantings.
The buildings are beautiful and the new student center is an amazing space.
The sports facilities are great and if you have the chance you should try to get down there for a game whether it's football, basketball , water polo or even rugby. No matter what sport you go to see, it's always a great time.
The staff and the students are always friendly and welcoming !
After you graduate, the connection doesn't end there. The alumni association is strong and holds events all over the country.
We were in Florida and the Fordham baseball team was playing Florida Atlantic University and Fordham had an alumni tailgate at FAU before the game !
Homecoming weekend is a great time to be on campus. The tent on Edwards Parade is a great time as is the tailgate lot which is packed with Fordham pride.
Homecoming always starts with the Ram Run which I proudly run each year.
Academically, Fordham is stronger than ever ! Besides Rose Hill there is the Lincoln Center campus, the London Campus, the Westchester campus and even a biological field station in Westchester.
Fordham also nurtures a students spiritual needs. The campus ministry is strong and well rounded. The campus church is beautiful and we attend Christmas Eve Mass there each year.
Yes the tuition is expensive but you get what you pay for.  The university just received a  $100 million donation to build a new STEM building and increase the schools offerings I'm the sciences.
The school offers a wide array of undergrad and post grad degrees and the networking of the alums allows for greater job opportunities upon graduation.
Look, no school is perfect but Fordham is a fine example of Jesuit higher education and deserves a look from anyone considering higher education.
Take a look at Fordham and join the Ramily!!!

This is a beautiful place with an exceptional atmosphere and excellent service. The ambiance is truly one of the highlights—everything feels thoughtfully designed, elegant, and inviting, and the overall experience is wonderful.

Some of the dishes we tried were very well executed and absolutely delicious. In particular, the Butternut Squash Soup was incredibly good—probably one of the best dishes we had, and I would highly recommend it. The Tempura Shiitakes were also excellent and definitely among our favorites.

That said, some of the other dishes felt a little too focused on presentation rather than flavor. The main courses are very creative and beautifully presented, but some of them fall slightly short in terms of taste. There is also a tendency to use quite a lot of sugar, including in some of the desserts, which makes them feel overly sweet and somewhat heavy on the palate.

Overall, I think there is a lot of creativity and care in the presentation, but the flavors could be a little more balanced and refined. Still, the atmosphere, service, and overall setting are absolutely wonderful, and the Butternut Squash Soup and Tempura Shiitakes alone are worth trying.

First of all, I would like to express my sincere appreciation to the chef and the entire staff at Le Coucou. The food was delicious, the service was warm and attentive, and the atmosphere was wonderful.
I visited Le Coucou to celebrate my birthday. I wasn't expecting any grand gestures or special surprises. Instead, each staff member who came by our table took a moment to sincerely wish me a happy birthday. That alone was more than enough to make the evening feel special.

Bread & Butter
The sourdough bread and butter were excellent. The quality of something as simple as bread and butter was more than enough to remind me that I was dining at a proper French restaurant.

Leeks
The leek appetizer was beautifully balanced. It had a subtle acidity, the natural sweetness of the vegetables, restrained seasoning, a refreshing quality, and just the right amount of texture.
To me, it fulfilled everything I look for in an appetizer: something that awakens the palate without overwhelming it.

Sweetbreads
The sweetbreads were tender and cooked just right. They had a rich, delicate offal flavor without being overpowering.
The sauce complemented them beautifully, and I particularly enjoyed the mushrooms served alongside them.

Rabbit
The rabbit was presented in several preparations: meat accompanied by a salad, a clear broth, and tender meat and onions gently cooked with mustard.
(I’m referring to them simply as "meat" because, although I have some guesses about the cuts, I’m not entirely certain.)
It was a worthwhile experience for someone interested in trying rabbit. The kitchen handled the distinctive flavor of rabbit very well, keeping it pleasantly subtle.
That said, while I enjoyed the dish, I felt it fell just a little short of being truly exceptional in terms of flavor.

Duck & Figs
Finally, the duck and fig dish.
The first thing I tasted was the duck breast. I had seen some reviews describing it as tough, but my experience was quite different.
What impressed me most was how I perceived three distinct textures and flavors:
Breast: Pleasantly chewy, with a pronounced, satisfying duck flavor.
Leg: Tender, with a richer expression of the duck's fat.
Liver: Exceptionally soft, with a deep, concentrated richness characteristic of offal.
Rather than competing with one another, these three elements felt like carefully constructed layers, each offering something distinct.
The figs were another highlight. Their natural sweetness complemented the duck so beautifully that they effectively served as an excellent sauce on their own.

Final Thoughts
Le Coucou offers a wonderful atmosphere, and its staff are both genuinely kind and highly professional. The food also provides an excellent opportunity to explore ingredients, flavors, and preparations that may be unfamiliar to many diners.
Not every dish was equally memorable, but the overall experience was thoughtful, enjoyable, and absolutely worth having.
Most importantly, the warmth and sincerity of the staff made my birthday dinner feel special without the need for any elaborate celebration.
Thank you to the chef and the entire team at Le Coucou for giving me such a wonderful evening.

My husband and I were visiting from out of town and were genuinely excited to try this restaurant for the first time. While the food itself was good, the service and overall atmosphere completely ruined our experience.

Throughout our visit, we noticed servers speaking among themselves in another language while pointing in our direction, laughing, and making comments. I want to make it very clear that speaking another language was never the issue. What made us uncomfortable was the pointing, laughing, and behavior that made us feel as though we were being mocked or talked about.

At one point, my husband spoke a few words to me in Spanish, and the servers began laughing again. Given everything we had already observed, it made the situation feel even more uncomfortable and disrespectful.

The experience became even more upsetting when we went to pay. The restaurant only accepted cash or Venmo, so my husband paid through Venmo. When the server returned, my husband told him that the payment had been sent. The server looked at the amount and said, “Only $27?” As we were walking away, we heard him call my husband a “cheapass.”

That comment was completely inappropriate and disrespectful. Customers should never be insulted by staff, especially after paying for their meal. If the restaurant expected a different amount, the server could have addressed it professionally instead of making a personal insult.

I cannot say with certainty what was being said during the rest of our visit, but the pointing, laughing, and final comment were enough to make us feel unwelcome and singled out. As customers, no one should have to sit through a meal wondering whether the staff is making fun of them or treating them differently because of their background.

What makes this even more disappointing is that we came in with genuine excitement to enjoy the food, the culture, and the experience. Instead, we left feeling uncomfortable and disrespected.

Good food means very little when the people serving it make customers feel unwelcome. Hospitality is about more than what comes out of the kitchen. It’s about how you treat the people who choose to support your business.

Unfortunately, what should have been a memorable dining experience for all the right reasons became memorable for all the wrong ones. We left incredibly disappointed and would not return.

The soul of the restaurant is Danish chef Ronny Emborg. His cuisine clearly carries Nordic/Scandinavian influences:

* Seafood and fish are prominently featured.

* Extensive use of fermentation, smoking, herbs, and acidity.

* Refined dishes that aren't simply piled high with caviar and truffles.

* Emphasis on aroma, temperature, texture, and complexity.

* The menu is constantly evolving.

Currently, the tasting menu is $325 per person, and it's seasonal and continuously evolving. Full payment is required upon reservation. Perhaps due to this system, reservations are relatively easy to secure among Michelin-starred restaurants; you'll generally get a table a day in advance.

I've been there twice, once I was met with super rude behavior and decided that the food was decent enough that I would go again to support a Chinese institution. ==Food Quality==
I haven't posted a review in a long time but I felt the need to be fair and let people know. I grew up in a Chinatown and have traveled to Hong Kong, Guangzhou, San Francisco, Toronto, etc., and even Milan. Know a historical Chinatown in the US? I've probably stopped by. I know what good roast duck/roast pork tastes like.

They say that they use an "older method" of making the food here to do things the hard way. The result is that it's about just as good as many of the other popular NYC roast duck/pork places with some others being better.

==Cleanliness==
This is where more modern restaurants in Chinatown shine. There's more attention to detail. More likely to keep the tables clean, more likely to wipe down after chopping things, etc. Great NY Noodletown has also been the subject of a pretty high-profile NYC shutdown. And this is the city that basically gives every restraurant an A rating.

==Atmosphere==
The place is small and the counter is chaotic. I've been here multiple times and this has been the case. Influencers have popularized this place and has made this place less manageable for the front of house.

==Service==
This is where I'm most disappointed. I didn't need to dine in, I just wanted to wait for a half duck to go which is premade, and gets chopped on the spot.

They end up skipping me.

Upon telling them that I was there first the guy, on the phone, ended up yelling at me instead of apologizing asking "Then what did you want?"

Afterwards, he complains about me to my face thinking I can't understand him to his coworker. (spoiler I speak multiple dialects of Chinese.)

Then he ends up knocking on the table demanding the money after the duck was chopped and ready to go.

Not only was he in the wrong, he never apologized and even talked about me in my face thinking he could get away with it and then demanded money as if I wasn't going to pay.

Having enjoyed supplemental courses at Michelin-starred restaurants like Frevo, Jean-Georges, and The Modern, we expected something special. We visited Huso for a birthday celebration and unfortunately left with mixed feelings. The food presentation was beautiful, and the highlight of the meal was definitely the dessert inspired by a maple tree. It had multiple layers and different flavors, and the pecan ice cream paired with it was especially delicious and unique. We also appreciated the Polaroid photo taken for us, and one of the female servers was genuinely warm and kind enough to compliment us, which was a lovely touch.

However, the service was disappointing for a birthday dinner. We were still eating our dessert when the check was brought to us, and we were asked about it twice afterward. Since the dessert had just been served and we were clearly still eating, it made us feel rushed, almost as if we were being asked to leave. Our table was also right by the entrance and hallway, which made the seating feel less comfortable and special for a birthday occasion. One of the male servers came across as noticeably unfriendly throughout the evening, and our interactions with him felt rather cold and awkward.

There were also some issues with the food. The first course with caviar tasted quite fishy to both of us, and the tuna underneath looked unusually dark. I usually do not notice much fishiness in seafood, but the flavor was quite strong this time. One server also seemed to forget parts of the dish explanation while presenting it. Most of the dishes were visually impressive, but some were fairly underwhelming in flavor. We also noticed a strawberry in one of the desserts that looked wrinkled and not particularly fresh.

Overall, there were definitely some memorable dishes and thoughtful touches, especially the dessert and the Polaroid photo, but the service and a few food-quality issues made the birthday experience less enjoyable than we expected. It's comforting food that lets the ingredients shine.

The congees are a must-order! My favorites are the classic century egg and pork congee, boneless shredded chicken congee, and their special Sampan congee. They're hearty, comforting, and perfect when you're craving something warm and soothing.

I'm also a big fan of their beef chow fun. The noodles aren't overly oily, and they’re generous with the ingredients, which makes a big difference. Their house special fried rice is another standout for me. It's not greasy, and I love the addition of unique ingredients like tiny scallops that give it extra flavor and texture.

Overall, Noodle Village is a solid spot for classic Chinese comfort food without everything being drenched in oil or overloaded with salt. I loved everything!

The food was excellent, I especially loved the Thai stir-fried noodles, and the service was also exceptional.
Great coffee! And loved the unique flavors. Great service too, Dev and Luna were fantastic
Amazing service and Coffee!! Thanks Luna and Deb for your attention
Great place! Coffee is top!
Immaculate vibes. Visited for a happy hour with friends and loved everything.
What am incredible view. And the staff, nice and kind. Thank you and I hope to be able to visit again soon!

This was my group's spot for great vibes, views and drinks after work. The makeover it got wasn't exactly needed but is much appreciated between the decor, art and little things like the lamps & carafes/pitchers. The views have always been first class and the Azul on the roof is icing on the cake for more letting loose. The menu is loaded with options worth trying to quench the post work thirst and calm that hunger. Definitely a spot to check off having been to and then keep coming back.

Definitely a NYC hidden gem. Great vibe, music, view. The finger food is good and served fast. Drinks are nice. A place to totally unwind and relax after hectic day of work. Great 270 view of manhattan and hudson.

Bar Hugo is the perfect way to spend a summer evening in the city. The views, the vibes, and the food are all incredible, but the service is what truly sets it apart. The staff genuinely love being there, and that energy comes through in every interaction. Warm, attentive, and effortlessly good at what they do. If you live in NYC or are just visiting, this place is a must.

Finally returned here after many years to find that everything was just as good as we remembered.  The cozy romantic atmosphere, food, and service are all top notch.  The kassoulet is divine That’s my go to. That’s what I recommend.

This is a nice restaurant! Very quaint and quite large. I ordered the steak au poivre and my wife the tartar. We also shared a beet salad. The portion of the salad was quite small. The steak was more so a medallion, also doesn’t come with fries. It was very well cooked and good flavor. The drinks were quite good as well.
The food wasn't amazing, I was excited after the reviews and seeing reddit but it was average. Service was great.

If I could take pride in my work like Marty and Chef Didier do on a daily basis, my life would feel so full.

I'm so impressed by both of these two, as well as the hostess. This was a great experience I will be bringing my business team back to again. and again and again and again.

Ate here years ago and decided to come back and what a great decision it was. It’s such a cozy little restaurant with different rooms. Enzo was our waiter who was great we brought our own wine which means you have to pay the bill in cash which I didn’t mind with no corkage fee if you’re not bringing your own wine. Then you can pay by credit card. The escargot was fantastic, but the highlight of our appetizers was the ravioli with truffle cream sauce. The seared foie gras seemed expensive on the menu, but it was the largest portion foie gras I’ve ever seen and it was delicious. The rabbit in a mustard wine sauce was also very tasty as was the chocolate lava cake . I will definitely come back again one of the best meals I’ve had in a while.
Got a take out order it was decent!
Fish was not fresh and smelled odd
So fresh!!

Had the most amazing time. Local spot on Greenwich Street with an amazing bartender Cesar. The drinks (The Great Wall) were so good. The rolls and fried jasmine rice were delicious. It’s my new favorite local! Great view of the Freedom Tower and super comfortable chairs! Great staff! Wonderful experience!

I've been a diner at this restaurant for many years, ever sinve I worked on Lafayette Street off of Prince Street.  I'm vegan and having a vegan Asian restaurant nearby was helpful when I didn't have time to be home to prepare a meal.

The floor in the restaurant was sticky and dirty to the point where it resembled a raunchy night club floor after a long night serving syrupy sweet mixed drinks to jostling, previously inebriated revelers.

The tables are that kind of wood finish that ends up dirty and sticky as a result of the tops not being maintained properly and being wiped down with rags that were never sanitized and clean to begin with.

I ordered a "sizzling" platter which was served decidedly not "sizzling" but rather sizzling the way an earthwom "sizzles" in the dirt after a rainstorm passes and the bright sun bears down on the parched hard-packed surface the worm has had the misfortune of finding itself on the wrong side of.

The cook decided the best time to take out a bag of garbage was in the moments leading up to when I would be receiving my main course (the flacid, tepid pile of nearly uncooked saitan and undercooked tomatoes).   The guy walked by my table with a heavy black plastic bag bursting with food scraps and kitchen waste, hoisting it skyward like Perseus delivering the head of Medusa to the menacing sea monster.

The watress was couteous and attentive and the food was delivered in a timely manner and with an appropriate amount of skill expected from New York City waitstaff.  She had the appearance of some vestal virgin vainly attempting to keep the "eternal" flame lit as the temple slowly decays and collapese around her - the last of her kind full of hopefullness that the storefront will continue to accepet eager diners willing to part with their earnings plus tips in such a way that she can come close to supporting herself in a city with a severe housin crises that is not improving.  The neighborhood is gentrifying and I would say their lease will be renewed in such a way that it describes improvements to the surrounding properties.

It is sad to say that this particular venue has seen its best days past and is beginning to show signs of wear and neglect and a degraded clientele.  It might be best to sign off in such a way that the remaining loyal customers come away with fond memories and regret that that little vegan Asian restaurant where they used to go is no longer there.

This has been a staple for years. Used to get takeout all the time when I worked nearby, now I pop in whenever possible for a great sit-down meal. The fact that it's still thriving in the same location for so long is proof that it's yum.

A consistent neighborhood restaurant with solid food, service, and atmosphere.

We ordered the Delhi Style Bhalla Papdi Chaat, Crispy Eggplant, Masala Potato Chaat, and Aloo Tikki Chaat to start. Everything hit the spot.

We also ordered a number of curries, including the Baingan Bharta, Chana Masala, Alleppy Fish Curry, Butter Chicken, and Chicken Tikka Masala, along with some sides and breads.

We went to Paisley for our anniversary and left already planning our return.

The food was delicious, especially the Chicken Chettinad, where coconut, fennel, black pepper, and mustard seeds came together in a warm, layered heat that tingled without overwhelming. The garlic naan was about as perfect as naan gets: light, airy, warm, and full of flavor.

The cocktails were just as impressive, with generous pours and intricate flavors. The Heart Beet was earthy and bright, and the Drop the Beet was smoky with a gentle kick.

The Mango Misu was a standout dessert. Silky mango mousse, a bright berry compote, and soft mango jelly made for a cool, refreshing finish that balanced the spice and never felt heavy.

The best part was the service, from start to finish. It felt welcoming and genuine, the kind of place where you can picture it becoming your regular spot. The owner and her husband were absolutely lovely. They made a point of wishing us a happy anniversary and stopped to chat with us, and it reminded me of a bygone era of real hospitality. It has the warmth of a mom-and-pop place inside a modern Manhattan restaurant, where you wouldn't expect to find it.

Definitely a gem. We'll be back for sure.

I just had the best Indian cuisine dinner here in Tribeca, New York. If you long to try for an authentic taste of New Delhi, Paisley is the name and the place you don’t want to miss. The food is great, Cocktails the best!! the place, ambiance, the feel and the staffs are all professional and superb service. 5 stars and Thumbs up for all the management. Highly recommended.👍🏻👏🏻🙌🏻😋😊🫡👌🏻

Ordered the dumplings and these are the best dumplings I ever had in this area. They’re really outstanding!  Been to few other places in NYC CT , and there’s no comparison. Can’t comment on their other items since I only order dumplings.

Very disappointed about my experience on a recent Sunday afternoon. Ordered 2 servings of chicken rice, beef noodle soup, lamb noodle soup, and dumplings. I waited 40 minutes for my food. I understand there was only one lady working, but it was a Sunday afternoon when food court is at its busiest. They should’ve put another person on. I saw other people waiting for a long time as well. If it was going to take 40 minutes for my food, it should’ve been made known to me right after I ordered (ordered on kiosk) and while I was standing near the stall.

Additionally, the food is subpar. I got their dumplings many times. That’s always been good. Noodle soups were okay. You can definitely find better at other places. Chicken rice that I waited 40 mins for (the lady told me she had to fry them and hence why it took so long) was the most disappointing. I had to even throw a serving away uneaten. The chicken was too soggy and fatty. Flavor had potential.

I hate to leave a bad review on a small business but I’m hoping they see these low reviews recently and improve in the areas they need to. I recently saw a new branch of theirs somewhere else other than Chinatown so they are definitely expanding, but I believe this stall was the original location. Very disappointing as I used to come here to get their dumplings all the time when I lived in Chinatown.
Got the beef noodles. Noodles were unfortunately way overcooked and too soggy, rest of the ingredients were also only ok
Delicious! 😋 We ate our fill for only 18 yuan per person!

Easy to find on Bowey st. In Manhattan's Chinatown (1/2 block south of the iconic Canal st). Looks a little plain on the outside. They sport roasted ducks in the windows (which is a famous look, in many NYC Chinatown restaurants). The restaurant has a "box car" layout. There are about 5 family style tables ( holding 8 - 10 people) and an additional 3-4 smaller, 1 or 2 person tables. The paper menu is huge and looks like a typical Chinese takeout menu. The options are tremendous and have many styles to choose from. Each table starts with a customery endless pot of tea. The speed and serving sizes was surprising. We were a table of 6 and in about 10 minutes, the orders started coming out to us. Everyone was served within 15 minutes. My friends ordered chicken and pork, beef and seafood dishes. My friend Jenny (a Manhattan Chinatown born and raised native) ordered seafood on crispy noodles. She shared  some with 3 of us and still had alot for herself. I tasted one of the shrimps. It was a big tasty shrimp, marinated in congee sauce. I was surprised there was so much, in an individual serving plate. Another person ordered a wonton noodle dish, which looked like a 2 - 3 pound bowl. I  bet she couldn't finish it (although she did). MY MEAL; I ordered the roasted duck (seoi siu aap - in Cantonese) on white rice. Like the others, my meal came out in about 10 minutes and was a huge dish. There were 10 large pieces of duck layed, on a fluffy bed of white rice, with a sided of steamed vegetables. The duck was a bit plain. Although, when I added "THEIR" soy sauce on it, the flavour was better. I said "THEIR" soy sauce because, it was sweeter than most soy sauces and it was a "tad" bit thicker. This is a soy sauce you'll want to take home. Actually, the fact that the duck came without sauce is a good thing. I've had  duck in the past and the sauce did not always agree to my liking. The meat was tender and succulent. On the whole, it was better than"marginally good" Be clear, I definitely enjoyed it down to the last bite. It just didn't stand out from the other roasted duck dishes out there. A strange (still ok) thing; there weren't any fortune cookies? 🤔They did however, have "Chinese doughnuts" - for $2.50. It's an oversized wobbly shaped doughnut, 3X the size of a normal doughnut with confectionery sugar. This was a first for me, it being more a novelty. The big shock, was the bill. With separate checks, I had roasted duck on white rice and a Chinese beer. With tax, the bill came out to $14.50! With what I got, I  thought this was going to be a $20 bill,( just for the food alone). My friend Jenny said, at the end of the meal, this restaurant is her favorite. She explained, she always has enough leftovers, to take home and the price is great. This restaurant is a few blocks away from the court houses in lower Manhattan and can get predictably crowded, during the lunch hour. We went on a Sunday, with mostly families at the other tables. We got a table immediately. The kitchen was small and well kept. It was nice to see my meals were coming from a properly kept kitchen. Whilst dining, the kitchen brought out bulk items of food, were they assemble the meals, up front, by the window, for take out orders. This is a fun way to see what else is on the menu. The waiters are all Chinese, speaking Cantonese and Mandarin. If they stumble on English, there's always someone there to help. Please please don't be insulted by their manners, as sometimes they come off abrupt and short (even if you are Chinese). It's a Chinese/Chinatown restaurant "thing". Throughout time, I've become used to it and I don't even notice there manners anymore. Come tip time, I still give a generous tip anyway (they're still hard working people, with small wages).
Dine in or takeout, check out NB Wing Wong, you'll be happy.
P.S. Their online prices are higher than their  in person prices.

The food was absolutely amazing the most authentic food I've ever had in America, everyone was super nice and the food came very quick and is priced nicely. I had saw photos of food from Google Maps and ordered off the menu for the combination someone had on Google Maps and they were very accommodating with a good price. A fantastic discovery at Stone Street Café!

A charming spot where everything is in place for a wonderful time: a wide selection of sweet and savory dishes and a great selection of coffees roasted fresh on-site.

The atmosphere is particularly pleasant, with a cozy, relaxing interior and an outdoor terrace, ideal for unwinding, enjoying a good coffee, or even working quietly.

An authentic place, with a rich history and plenty of personality, where you'll want to linger and return. A must-try in New York! 🇺🇸✨

Comfortable shared tables in the back, solo seats and tables against the wall, and traditional seating in the front.

Everyone is in good enough mood, employees, families and youbg post college workers, and looking good.

The expresso banana bread is balanced, all the flavors show through. People are eating food here all the time, and I spot regulars.

A restaurant serving delicious, authentic sushi. The place is clean, prices are good, and the food arrives quickly. I was there with my daughters, and we really enjoyed it.

Love this place! Bright, and work friendly despite the ubiquitous music that seems unavoidable these days. The staff are lovely and the coffee and food are very good.

I’ve been a regular at The Lost Draft in Chinatown, and I’ve genuinely loved this place. I’ve always been respectful of their two-hour policy, consistently ordering drinks at least every two hours, often with a pastry, and tipping 20% or more. I’ve even contributed positive messages to their wall because I genuinely appreciate the concept and atmosphere they’ve created for film and theater artists.

Unfortunately, today’s experience left me feeling quite disappointed.

I needed to step outside briefly to take a phone call. Despite there being plenty of empty tables inside, a staff member came outside specifically to tell me that I needed to move my belongings from the four-person table I was occupying to a smaller one. I explained that I would be back in just a few minutes, but he insisted that I move my things immediately.

I understand that businesses have seating policies, and I have no problem respecting reasonable rules. What bothered me was the manner in which this was communicated. The staff member came across as unnecessarily rigid, unfriendly, and lacking in basic understanding, especially given that the café was far from full.

What makes this particularly disappointing is how much I’ve appreciated and supported this place. I’ve consistently respected their policies and contributed to the welcoming atmosphere they’re trying to cultivate. I don’t expect special treatment for being a regular, but I do think every customer deserves to be treated with basic courtesy and a little flexibility.

It’s a shame when a place with such a thoughtful, lovely concept falls short in the way it treats its customers. A welcoming atmosphere isn’t just about the décor, the drinks, or the messages on the wall. It’s also about how people are made to feel.

I still appreciate what The Lost Draft is trying to create, but today’s interaction made me feel considerably less welcome in a place I’ve genuinely enjoyed spending time in.

I almost walked right past this place, but something told me to double back and I'm so glad I did! It's tucked inside a food court, making it a bit of a hidden gem.
I ordered the baked brûlée milk latte, and it was absolutely delicious. It is rich, creamy, and perfectly balanced. It's the kind of drink I'd happily come back for. Next on my list is the taro slush!
They also have ube, black sesame, and green tea ice cream, which are some of my favorite flavors, so I'm already planning my next visit. If you're looking for a unique drink or dessert spot, this one is definitely worth checking out. I'll definitely be back!

I honestly don't understand the positive reviews because my experience was the complete opposite.
From the moment I walked into Zhen Pin Café, the manager/barista was rude, unwelcoming, and acted as though my presence was an inconvenience. I stood waiting without anyone offering to help me, and when I finally asked for assistance, I still didn't receive professional customer service.
I specifically ordered a jasmine latte, but I was served something completely different. When I politely pointed out the mistake, instead of apologizing or offering to remake the drink, the person became angry and argumentative. It was incredibly uncomfortable and completely unprofessional.
On top of that, the café did not appear clean during my visit. Based on what I observed, the overall cleanliness and sanitation of the establishment left me with a poor impression and made me question the attention to detail throughout the business.
Customer service, professionalism, and cleanliness are the basics of running any café, and unfortunately this place fell short in all three. I left feeling disappointed and unwelcome. I won't be returning, and I can't recommend this café based on my experience..

I guess I will stick with Starbucks, where the customer service is top notch & also the product is quality & sanitary.

This is exactly what you want from a sit down Chinese restaurant. Delicious, American Chinese food (unless you can read the Chinese menu and unlock the interesting stuff) done very, very well.

We had the beef chow fun and the lychee pineapple duck.

The chow fun was dang near perfect. The only note I have is that it was a drop salty. Otherwise, perfect. The wok hei (that hard to quantify smoky flavor when you get really good Chinese food) is always what brings this dish together, and it was really kicking in this disk. The beef was tender but not falling apart, a good bite but not chewy. The bean sprouts were crisp and satisfying.

The duck was really a work of art. It's a very fatty dish, but the fat under the skin was perfectly rendered, and it melted in my mouth. The sauce was sweet without being sickly, and mixed very well with the white rice that came in the side. The skin on the duck was excellent. It's tossed in a sauce so it's not crispy, but it was so savory and flavorful.

Almoçamos no Hop Kee em uma sexta-feira e gostei bastante da experiência. Escolhi conhecer o restaurante principalmente porque Anthony Bourdain esteve lá em um de seus programas, e eu adoro conhecer os lugares que aparecem nas experiências gastronômicas que ele mostrou em Nova York.

Pedimos alguns pratos e, para mim, o destaque foi a lagosta, que estava deliciosa. O arroz e a carne com brócolis também estavam muito bons, e o chá estava uma delícia.

Já o caranguejo à cantonês não me agradou tanto. O molho tinha muitas cartilagens, o que acabou tornando o prato um pouco difícil de comer.

O atendimento foi rápido e educado, e o ambiente tem aquele estilo tradicional de restaurante chinês, sem muita firula.

Importante: o pagamento é somente em dinheiro.

No geral, gostei bastante da experiência e, principalmente, de conhecer um restaurante tão tradicional e que fez parte de um dos programas do Bourdain.

Overall, it is a worthwhile place to enjoy cigars while taking in the character of Soho.

Medium size selection amazing service. I heard it was the oldest cigar lounge in Manhattan. All the staff were just so helpful and knowledgeable. Definitely can’t wait to come back. This will be one of my regular stops in the city.

Today, I had a regrettable experience while shopping at 194 Canal St. Due to an urgent need, I asked a uniformed employee if I could use the restroom, and they immediately said, "There is no restroom." However, a young white man not in uniform immediately came out, and the employee explained that he was an employee.

As a customer, I understand that businesses may have a policy of "restrooms not open to the public," but the employee's dismissive "there is none" and inconsistent approach made my family and me feel discriminated against and disrespected. Taipan Bakery is a trusted brand, and I hope management will prioritize employee communication training so that they can respond more honestly and empathetically to customer requests for assistance.

Service was super quick, and everyone was really nice, from the server to our barista. I decided to try one of their seasonal drinks, the Iced Pumpkin Spice Draft Latte with oat milk. Their Draft Latte is a creamy, smooth cold coffee drink, and the pumpkin spice gives it that warm seasonal flavour without completely overpowering the coffee. The oat milk also made it extra smooth and creamy. Definitely a nice fall drink.
My friends tried a few different drinks as well:
Matcha Vanilla — The matcha was actually really good, with a nice balance between the earthy matcha and sweetness from the vanilla. Neither flavour overpowered the other.
Caramel Apple Latte — A nice combination of coffee, caramel and apple flavours. It had a good balance of sweetness and coffee, with the apple adding a subtle fruity touch rather than making it taste overly sweet.
Iced Vanilla Latte — Pretty much true to its name! A straightforward iced latte with a clear vanilla flavour. Simple, refreshing, and exactly what you'd expect.
The café itself was clean and has a smaller, cozy setup with around 7 stools for seating, along with a bench running along the entire back wall. It seems like a good spot to grab a quick coffee or sit for a little while.
Overall, a quick and pleasant visit with friendly service and a good selection of drinks. The seasonal Pumpkin Spice Draft Latte was definitely a fun one to try.

First of all, I would like to express my sincere appreciation to the chef and the entire staff at Le Coucou. The food was delicious, the service was warm and attentive, and the atmosphere was wonderful.
I visited Le Coucou to celebrate my birthday. I wasn't expecting any grand gestures or special surprises. Instead, each staff member who came by our table took a moment to sincerely wish me a happy birthday. That alone was more than enough to make the evening feel special.

Bread & Butter
The sourdough bread and butter were excellent. The quality of something as simple as bread and butter was more than enough to remind me that I was dining at a proper French restaurant.

Leeks
The leek appetizer was beautifully balanced. It had a subtle acidity, the natural sweetness of the vegetables, restrained seasoning, a refreshing quality, and just the right amount of texture.
To me, it fulfilled everything I look for in an appetizer: something that awakens the palate without overwhelming it.

Sweetbreads
The sweetbreads were tender and cooked just right. They had a rich, delicate offal flavor without being overpowering.
The sauce complemented them beautifully, and I particularly enjoyed the mushrooms served alongside them.

Rabbit
The rabbit was presented in several preparations: meat accompanied by a salad, a clear broth, and tender meat and onions gently cooked with mustard.
(I’m referring to them simply as "meat" because, although I have some guesses about the cuts, I’m not entirely certain.)
It was a worthwhile experience for someone interested in trying rabbit. The kitchen handled the distinctive flavor of rabbit very well, keeping it pleasantly subtle.
That said, while I enjoyed the dish, I felt it fell just a little short of being truly exceptional in terms of flavor.

Duck & Figs
Finally, the duck and fig dish.
The first thing I tasted was the duck breast. I had seen some reviews describing it as tough, but my experience was quite different.
What impressed me most was how I perceived three distinct textures and flavors:
Breast: Pleasantly chewy, with a pronounced, satisfying duck flavor.
Leg: Tender, with a richer expression of the duck's fat.
Liver: Exceptionally soft, with a deep, concentrated richness characteristic of offal.
Rather than competing with one another, these three elements felt like carefully constructed layers, each offering something distinct.
The figs were another highlight. Their natural sweetness complemented the duck so beautifully that they effectively served as an excellent sauce on their own.

Final Thoughts
Le Coucou offers a wonderful atmosphere, and its staff are both genuinely kind and highly professional. The food also provides an excellent opportunity to explore ingredients, flavors, and preparations that may be unfamiliar to many diners.
Not every dish was equally memorable, but the overall experience was thoughtful, enjoyable, and absolutely worth having.
Most importantly, the warmth and sincerity of the staff made my birthday dinner feel special without the need for any elaborate celebration.
Thank you to the chef and the entire team at Le Coucou for giving me such a wonderful evening.

Little Italy is one of those New York neighborhoods where, every once in a while, you find a place that feels like a passage to the past, and Caffe Roma is exactly that.

Founded in 1891, this cafe has managed to preserve something that is increasingly difficult to find in New York: the feeling of another era. In the middle of all the noise, movement, and constant change of the city, stepping inside feels like entering a little time capsule. And yes, the coffee is excellent, but Caffe Roma is about more than just coffee.

Take a moment to look around. The details on the walls, the ceiling, the old-fashioned décor... they are all part of the experience. This place has been collecting stories for more than a century, and you can feel that history while sitting at your table, enjoying a coffee and an Italian dessert. With just a little imagination, you might even travel back in time for a few minutes.

My personal favorite is the affogato. I love the combination of hot espresso and cold, creamy vanilla gelato, and this is exactly the kind of place where it just feels right to order one.

When I came back to the store, the staff told me she thought I said “葡萄啵啵,” because apparently THEY call the grape slush “葡萄啵啵” at this store. But this was literally my first time here. How am I supposed to know that?? I clearly said 葡萄多多, and I even specifically asked for a LARGE. As you can see from the menu in the photo, the Yakult series DOES come in a large size, so there was nothing unusual or confusing about me ordering a large 葡萄多多. I never said 葡萄啵啵 or 葡萄冰沙.

And honestly, the grape slush tasted terrible too. It basically tasted like flavorless blended ice with some grape syrup poured into it. That was it. I definitely would never have ordered this drink on purpose.

What made the whole experience even worse was the attitude when I came back. The staff very reluctantly agreed to remake my drink, but instead of fixing the order they got wrong, she continued making drinks for people who ordered after me first. It honestly made me feel like I was asking for a free drink or causing trouble, when I had already paid and was only asking for the drink I actually ordered.

I waited for more than 10 minutes and eventually had to leave because I had an appointment. So I paid for a drink I didn’t order, came all the way back to get it corrected, waited again, and still left without the drink I actually wanted.

There was only ONE staff member working in the entire store, which clearly didn’t help, but the way this situation was handled was incredibly frustrating.

I definitely won’t be coming back to this location again.

Excellent in every phase. Cool bar vibe, excellent drinks. The menu is great with all sorts of high quality choices - pasta, steaks,

Great atmosphere, sandwiches are delicious and well priced.

I guess go here if you are desperate but other than the location there’s really nothing good about it. The service was slow, and the food was not up to par, to say the least. I probably won’t be back.

Delicious, hearty breakfast bagels and really fresh hot chocolate. Super nice employees, too, who keep the place spotless and orders running smoothly. A perfect on-the-go breakfast spot! 😋

Love editing a prior review for a positive!  Red snapper was perfectly crisped and flavor was balanced with just enough citrus notes.  New host (and/or manager) this evening and the service is very friendly and welcoming - perfect

We had a wonderful experience right up until the end.  Food was fantastic - great menu options, everything we ordered was delicious!  The service was brilliant at the start, and throughout the meal - only when we finished and wanted the check did things rapidly go downhill.  At maybe 30% capacity the waiter seemed to be struggling to keep up with tables (unsure if understaffed or just too many take-out orders or what) and it took ages to be able to get his attention.  When we did, he was moody about us needing to split the bill (2 of us, here on a business trip, so needed to pay separately for expenses claim) My colleague is English as a second language but their English is near perfect - I ended up assisting when it became clear that she was becoming flustered because the waiter was being so rude about her request to split the bill into a third part to cover alcohol that was out of scope of our expenses allowance - he even sarcastically declared "yeah take your time, I already split it once I can split it again, I don't have anything else to do" whilst walking away from us.  Maybe he was just having a particularly difficult shift, or a bad day, but it was a really disappointing end to a lovely meal.  The service we had up until that point was so good I can't bring myself to rate it any lower than 4 stars.

Really we had a couple tiny laptops, and maybe a small flat monitor and then 20 dollar store plates. Those go by really fast when you’re hitting them with a bat so I think they need more variety in their selection of items. We had a group and we had a fun time together (we do regardless), but I will say for the money I don’t think it’s worth it honestly, but now we know.

I also didn’t know they automatically build in tip/an admin fee so by the time a group of 12 of us went, it was nearly $1700 which is aggressive when each person is raging probably for 10-15 minutes.

Excellent and friendly staff. Service in the blink of an eye. Very helpful. Order was perfect.

If you live in Tribeca you can't not love Yves, a beloved neighborhood haunt, with great vibes, outdoor seating and a thematic decor depending on the season. Dolomites in the winter, French Riviera in the summer.

The food is great, and the cocktails even greater. My favorite was 'Je Suis un Rockstar' with Cardenxe Sotol.

One of my favorite restaurants in TriBeCa This Classic French style Bistro serving delicious and interesting menu options in wonderful Parisian style setting  with lively atmosphere , cool vibes & bar scene , providing wonderful service. Every time we visit it gets better & better .

The second you walk downstairs, the city just disappears. It's dark, lit almost entirely by candles, with old brick and stone all around you, and it feels like you've stepped into some hidden place from another time. Everything about it works on you at once: the flicker of candlelight on the water, the quiet music, the warmth of the pools, the shock of the cold plunge, the salt bath where you just float and forget where you are. It's not just a spa visit, it's a full experience for every sense, and I walked out feeling like a completely different person. Hands down the best experience I've ever had, and I'd recommend it to anyone without hesitating.

The location is quaint and charming, and the customer service was great! The banana cream cheese cupcake was delicious and definitely the standout. Unfortunately, the other cupcakes we tried were very dry and almost tasted a bit stale. It was later in the afternoon, so that may have played a part. Overall, I’d definitely stop back and get the banana cream cheese cupcake again!

Updated with a screenshot of one of my orders that had both chocolate frosting and chocolate filling, and another order that had vanilla and vanilla. And a picture online that shows a cake with chocolate on outside and chocolate filling as well. Again, this is my last order from Billy’s ever - extremely frustrating to be told over and over something was always a way when it was not.

Have ordered the crowd pleaser cake for years and it always lives up to its name. I’ve always ordered chocolate frosting on the outside with chocolate filling on the inside and everyone loves it and goes on to order it themselves. Went to order it again this week and it was not a choice to have chocolate filling inside if I chose chocolate outside (this has never happened before so it was a change). Reached out to customer service and was told over and over that it’s always been like this and it has to be that way - even after I sent screenshots of old orders. They said the frosting and the filling have always been the opposite and have to be that way. Really frustrating experience bc it simply hasn’t always been that way, and when I asked why they HAVE to be that way they said so the customer can experience both flavors. I requested over and over for the chocolate filling inside as I and most of the people this cake will be eaten by hate vanilla filling and have always LOVED the crowd pleaser chocolate frosting outside and Chocolate filling inside. The short rib appetizer is so fragrant, soft, charred and juicy. Definitely a meal-changer.
My Father-in-law’s swordfish schnitzel was crunchy, delicious.

They charge for bread. $5 a head. Our server asked after taking our order, we agreed. $25 extra dollars for the five of us. For bread at an Italian restaurant.

This is a fancier type of expensive restaurant, so the prices are expected to be on the higher side. That said, the food was very, very good. Must say, especially the T Bone steak ($190 for 30oz) which was cooked to absolute perfection. The homemade pasta they had was unique in flavor, texture and shape, in a good way. And the Funoccio salad was strong but was a great compliment to that T Bone steak. Desserts such as the Nectarine was something in gn we never had before and so glad we ordered it.
The waiter was very nice and offered good recommendations. The atmosphere was great as it had that New York sound in a fancy place.
Only thing is the chocolate cake we tried had much to be desired, as it was powdery and pretty dry. Flavor was more bitter and not sweet.
But everything else was top notch. Need a fancy place for dinner? Come here.

So, I asked if it would be possible to make my maple iced latte into a salted one and I offered to pay the extra amount. The barista was so nice to make it for me into a salted maple iced latte and I did not need to pay extra. I kinda wish I just stuck with the regular maple iced latte though.
Oh well. There are very few seating options in here. There were 2 tables I think if I remember correctly. I would come back here though and try out another drink.

Derby Cup Coffee is such a cool little spot and feels completely different from the typical NYC coffee shop. Love the old-school green awning, tiled floors, dark wood, plants everywhere and all the little details throughout the place. It has a ton of character and almost feels like you stumbled onto a neighbourhood spot that’s been there forever.

Really relaxed atmosphere inside, comfortable seating and a great place to sit down for a coffee without feeling rushed. The staff were friendly and the whole place just had a warm, laid-back vibe.

Definitely one of those places that catches your eye from the street and ends up being even cooler once you walk inside. Great little find in NYC and absolutely worth stopping in if you’re in the area.

Fun little place. We got a crepe cake, a couple drinks, and a mango mochi. All were decent. The matcha crepe cake was super soft but not as sweet as I expected, but that's just personal taste.

I recommend the fantastic Mango Cream Cube dessert. Clean. Very attentive service.
Incredibly fresh tasty food! The smoothies are amazing, the sandwiches are amazing, the bao so damn good! This place is fantastic and I can’t wait to go back again !
Delicious beyond burger with mango sauce!!

I love this place. I've been coming here for over 20 years. I live in the area and it is the local hangout that everyone goes to because the food is excellent, the wait staff is wonderful and the atmosphere is delightfully Retro and comfortable.

In Tribeca, a small neighborhood restaurant where you can find fabulous burgers and impeccable service. In summer, you can eat outside on a pleasant terrace where smoking is prohibited. Highly recommended.
Great food even better environment and close to the ghosts busters building
Food was amazing. Julian was amazing. We loved everything about it. Definitely come to this place. It will not disappoint And the specials are fantastic.
Strongly recommend absolutely delicious. Great food. Great ambience amazing prices.
Me gustó mucho este lugar, los chicos de la entrada muy amables. 10/10 🙌🏼💖
Top notch.
Fantastic!

I was a paying customer, had permission to use the restroom, and was inside for less than five minutes. From the moment we walked in the door at Eulalie, we knew we were in for a special evening.

From the lighting, to the colors, the decor, the jazz soundtrack at the perfect volume, and the generous table sizes and spacing; this is a meticulously designed and exceptionally comfortable room. It inspired me to take out my camera.

Even the acoustics were notable, either due to some kind of engineering wizardry, or because it’s just a room with good bones. At its busiest, it wasn’t noisy. And towards the end of the night, it wasn’t echoey or empty sounding.

The staff were fantastic. Everyone there truly seemed to enjoy what they were doing. Within a few minutes of sitting down, we were made to feel like regulars, even though this was our first visit.

Our main waiter Bennett, is a real renaissance man. Part waiter, part sommelier, part mâitre fromager. He and the rest of the team perfectly balanced professional and fun.

Little gifts appeared throughout the night… an extra wine pour here, some champagne there, amuses, an extra dessert.

The food was fantastic overall. The cheeses were sublime. The wine pairing we did was among the most inventive and thoughtful we’ve ever experienced.

The coconut cake was excellent but the pot de crème was a show stopper.

We spent a delightful 3+ hours at Eulalie, which in no way felt long. I told our waiter that the entire experience sort of felt like seeing a great off Broadway play and hanging out with the cast after the show. We laughed with chef Chip and his kitchen. We toasted with Tina. It was an extended whirlwind of culinary magic and tastefully choreographed joy.

On reflection, it also occurred to me that I got the same feels from dining at Eulalie as I did from watching Big Night. I can’t really think of a higher compliment for a restaurant.

review_text:
First of all, I would like to express my sincere appreciation to the chef and the entire staff at Le Coucou. The food was delicious, the service was warm and attentive, and the atmosphere was wonderful.
I visited Le Coucou to celebrate my birthday. I wasn't expecting any grand gestures or special surprises. Instead, each staff member who came by our table took a moment to sincerely wish me a happy birthday. That alone was more than enough to make the evening feel special.

Bread & Butter
The sourdough bread and butter were excellent. The quality of something as simple as bread and butter was more than enough to remind me that I was dining at a proper French restaurant.

Leeks
The leek appetizer was beautifully balanced. It had a subtle acidity, the natural sweetness of the vegetables, restrained seasoning, a refreshing quality, and just the right amount of texture.
To me, it fulfilled everything I look for in an appetizer: something that awakens the palate without overwhelming it.

Sweetbreads
The sweetbreads were tender and cooked just right. They had a rich, delicate offal flavor without being overpowering.
The sauce complemented them beautifully, and I particularly enjoyed the mushrooms served alongside them.

Rabbit
The rabbit was presented in several preparations: meat accompanied by a salad, a clear broth, and tender meat and onions gently cooked with mustard.
(I’m referring to them simply as "meat" because, although I have some guesses about the cuts, I’m not entirely certain.)
It was a worthwhile experience for someone interested in trying rabbit. The kitchen handled the distinctive flavor of rabbit very well, keeping it pleasantly subtle.
That said, while I enjoyed the dish, I felt it fell just a little short of being truly exceptional in terms of flavor.

Duck & Figs
Finally, the duck and fig dish.
The first thing I tasted was the duck breast. I had seen some reviews describing it as tough, but my experience was quite different.
What impressed me most was how I perceived three distinct textures and flavors:
Breast: Pleasantly chewy, with a pronounced, satisfying duck flavor.
Leg: Tender, with a richer expression of the duck's fat.
Liver: Exceptionally soft, with a deep, concentrated richness characteristic of offal.
Rather than competing with one another, these three elements felt like carefully constructed layers, each offering something distinct.
The figs were another highlight. Their natural sweetness complemented the duck so beautifully that they effectively served as an excellent sauce on their own.

Final Thoughts
Le Coucou offers a wonderful atmosphere, and its staff are both genuinely kind and highly professional. The food also provides an excellent opportunity to explore ingredients, flavors, and preparations that may be unfamiliar to many diners.
Not every dish was equally memorable, but the overall experience was thoughtful, enjoyable, and absolutely worth having.
Most importantly, the warmth and sincerity of the staff made my birthday dinner feel special without the need for any elaborate celebration.
Thank you to the chef and the entire team at Le Coucou for giving me such a wonderful evening.

My sibling had always raved about Mr. Chow, so we booked an 8:00 p.m. Friday birthday dinner at the Tribeca location. It was our first visit.

The restaurant was extremely loud because of what appeared to be a party or happy-hour event. Initially, all six of us were seated at a table intended for four adults, so we asked for a larger table. The staff then tried to seat us near the loud crowd, and we requested another move. Eventually, we were given an appropriately sized table away from the noise.

Family-Style Appetizers

The service was good; however, the food and its presentation were subpar.

·         Chicken Satay: Just okay.

·         Glazed Prawns (2): Great.

·         Vegetarian Potstickers: Just okay and served without dipping sauce.

Family-Style Entrées

·         Ma Mignon: Great.

·         Green Prawns: Good.

·         Sea Bass: Bad and very bland.

·         Beijing Chicken: Just okay.

Family-Style Sides

·         String Beans with XO Sauce: Good.

·         Vegetable Sautéed Rice: Good.

Overall Impression

We expected much more care to be given to the presentation. Every dish arrived simply arranged on a silver platter and lacked visual appeal. The flavors were also unremarkable.

Given the restaurant’s reputation, the experience was very disappointing. We would neither recommend Mr. Chow nor return as customers.
Way too overrated. The food wasn’t good at all, and I really didn’t like the minimum spending requirement. Definitely not worth it.

I don't know why, but I threw up twice during the night after eating; it was either food poisoning or something didn't agree with me.
Apparently, there is a $75 minimum spending requirement, and they applied this rule even to a 2-year-old baby; furthermore, they didn't count the $100 worth of drinks we each consumed toward that total. We felt like we were being scammed. The waiters really spoiled our mood with annoying comments every five minutes, asking things like, "Don't you want to order more food?" or "What do you mean?" We were drinking champagne and spending $100 per person, yet we ended up paying extra just because we fell short of the minimum spending limit—it’s a ridiculous place. In Europe, it would be a miracle if a restaurant with such a poor-quality menu and flavor profile managed to stay open. The food was truly mediocre and terrible.

Unfortunately, our experience at Mr Chow on Hudson Street was very disappointing, especially considering the prices.

When we ordered, we were persuaded to add a first-course appetizer because we were told there was a $75 minimum per person and our original order apparently did not meet the minimum. We went along with the recommendation, but the appetizer was extremely plain and had barely any lobster in it, so it definitely did not feel worth the additional cost.

The timing of the food was another major issue. Our main course came out, but the fried rice and vegetables took so long that we were basically finished with our main course by the time everything arrived. The vegetables did not come out until approximately 45 minutes after the main course. On top of the long wait, both the fried rice and vegetables were very plain and underwhelming.

We also ordered non-alcoholic drinks and were shocked to see that a fruit punch was $16, while the lemonade was $7 and tasted watered down. When we brought our concerns to our server, Jose, including the confusion surrounding whether the rice and vegetables were included and the price of the fruit punch, his response was essentially that we “didn’t understand” what he had explained.

We were then told that the non-alcoholic fruit punch was apparently equivalent in price to a mojito, which is what had been rung up on our bill—even though our drink contained no alcohol. Despite bringing all of these concerns to Jose’s attention, nothing was adjusted or corrected on our bill.

To make the experience even more uncomfortable, after we paid, we were still seated at our table and holding onto the bill when another server reached over me to take it. The interaction made us feel as though we were being rushed out of our seats immediately after paying. What made that especially strange was that the restaurant was not busy at all—the inside dining area was essentially empty, and we were seated outside—so there did not appear to be any need to rush us out.

Instead of feeling like our concerns were acknowledged or that we were valued as customers, we left feeling dismissed and rushed. For a restaurant requiring a $75 minimum per person and charging these prices, we expected significantly better food, timing, communication, and customer service.

Unfortunately, the experience did not come close to what we expected from Mr Chow, and we left extremely disappointed.

I've been to all 3-star restaurants in New York, not to mention in Portugal, France, SF. I've also been to Jungsik 3~4 times, before they received a Michelin star. I'll say that this most recent visit was the most disappointing and I'm baffled at how they're maintaining 3 stars. Our entire meal, we were rushed through each course. Our waiter kept hovering and kept prodding me to eat more quickly. I've never been treated like this at any Michelin star restaurant. He would also frequently interject to make sure we weren't touching or disturbing the decorations on the plating or eating things in the wrong order. I understand that the chef would appreciate guests eating the dishes with intention and mindfulness, but this was over the top. The forced pace was extremely unpleasant and ruined our evening. Also, I've never in my life been asked to leave or vacate a table at any 3-star Michelin restaurant? Other places seem to know and accept that if we're spending literally thousands of dollars on a meal, that we should be able to sit and enjoy our meal, and even perhaps linger after eating 10 courses. We weren't ready to end the evening, since it was for my friend's 30th birthday, so we literally just stood outside the restaurant after we were ushered out, for about another 20 minutes, standing in slightly chilly weather to finish catching up. We weren't even offered coffee or tea with dessert to sit and enjoy. Even as we were leaving, the dozens of waitstaff kept brusquely asking us to clear the walkway and stand off to the side. We also had asked the kitchen to hold onto some personal items, that we asked them to retrieve for us at the end of the night, and they also completely forgot or misplaced the items, so we were standing (yet again) by the hostess for another 10-15 minutes simply waiting for someone to notice. Honestly, the food was also quite salty across multiple courses, but overall good. Less impressive than previous visits - menu could use a revamp. I think I had the same uni rice dish 7~8 years ago.

Overall, service was pretty appalling.

The food was really amazing! Service was perfect and cosy atmosphere made for a very enjoyable moment. Highly recommend!!

My only complaint would be the requirement to tip ahead of time on tock. It feels wrong to ask to tip the service ahead of receiving it.

9.99/10. Incredible restaurant. The food was at its best; it's hard to pick a single best dish. They also have top-notch service, an extensive wine list and an elegant ambience. Leo helped us choose the wine, and it worked perfectly. The 0.01 point I took off was because it wasn't clear when we should have ordered the supplementary dish we were really interested in (Uni bibimbap), and by the time we asked, it was too late.

Jungsik is undoubtedly an impressive culinary experience, and the cuisine is the strongest part of the evening.

The dishes were beautifully executed and presented with exceptional attention to detail. Flavors were deep, complex and very carefully balanced. For me, the standout was the opening sequence of banchan — genuinely memorable and one of the highlights of the entire dinner. There was a great sense of creativity and precision in the food.

Having dined at a number of three-Michelin-starred restaurants, however, I found the service at Jungsik somewhat below the level I have come to expect at this category of restaurant. Everyone was perfectly polite and professional, but at this level, hospitality is about more than being courteous and explaining the ingredients. At restaurants such as Noma, Geranium, Disfrutar or L’Arpège, I have experienced a much more natural interaction with the guests — a feeling that the team is genuinely engaging with you and reading the table, rather than simply delivering the service.

A small detail, but one that I found particularly unfortunate, was receiving the bill while I was still drinking my coffee. In a restaurant of this caliber, I would expect the end of the meal to feel completely unhurried. Instead, it gave me the impression that the table was ready to be turned over and that I should leave.

I also noticed that as the dining room became busier, the movement of the service team became noticeably faster and somewhat nervous. This created a sense of urgency that, in my opinion, does not quite fit the atmosphere I expect from a three-star dining room, where service should ideally feel calm, effortless and almost invisible.

The desserts were, for me, the least convincing part of the menu. As with everything else, the presentation was impeccable, but the flavors did not leave the same impression as the savory courses.

Overall, Jungsik delivers an excellent and highly refined culinary experience. The food absolutely demonstrates the level of ambition and technical precision expected from a restaurant of this stature. For me, however, the hospitality did not quite reach the same level as the cuisine. And once the food is operating at such a high level, it is precisely these seemingly small details of service that make the difference between an excellent dinner and a truly exceptional three-star experience.
Amazing!!!!!!

Overhyped, underwhelming, and absolutely not the "best happy hour in NYC" experience we were promised. We stopped by Arlo Rooftop at Arlo SoHo for anniversary cocktails and appetizers before dinner, and the service was so poor we left after one round. Great concept, disappointing execution.

The ambiance: The rooftop itself has potential, with a mix of lounge seating, high-tops, open space, greenery, and string lights. The interior felt a bit empty, but the rooftop could be a nice setting for drinks.

The experience:

* Seating: We arrived around 4:15 PM on a Friday to a very light crowd and were seated at a table that was legitimately in a bush. We politely asked to move to the adjacent table, only to be told it was reserved for a party arriving in 2.5 hours. I explained we planned to stay only an hour or two, but there was zero flexibility or effort to accommodate us. Not a great first impression.
* Drinks: My husband ordered a happy hour beer, and I ordered the Vinho Verde from the main menu, which was their most expensive drink option. Given the light crowd, our anniversary reservation, and the fact that we weren't exclusively ordering from the happy hour menu, I expected a little more attentiveness.
* Service: We waited 20 minutes without receiving either drink. I eventually walked inside to check on them, at which point our waitress noticed me and gestured toward the bartender. The drinks finally arrived a few minutes later. The Vinho Verde tasted off to me, almost as though the bottle had been open too long, though I can't say for certain.
* Follow-up: The most frustrating part? We weren't checked on again. Not once. We would have happily ordered another round and some appetizers, but after about an hour with our waitress having acknowledged us only once, we decided to leave.

Bottom line: we got an awkward table, a 20-minute wait for drinks, and virtually nonexistent service. The setting has potential, but hospitality matters just as much as the view.

Tastes great but the crab was particularly involved to peel and the duck was very bony. Otherwise, the space was reasonably quiet and got a generous table for a party of 4. Staff also seems Chinese first, so probably not recommended for non Chinese speakers

Easily some of the best cream puffs I’ve ever had. I got the taro and the matcha, and both had the perfect balance of light, airy pastry and decadent cream without being overly sweet. Great service and atmosphere, too. Can’t wait to come back!

Super friendly staff. They have expanded their desserts section to be more in line with their main store on 51st and 8th. The cream puff shell seemed to have been upgraded in thickness as well. It's been two days in the fridge and the shell is still crispy. They are supposed to be offering more beverages soon. Can't wait. This location is much less crowded, but it is without seating. Baked good prices start around $5.

Super cute sweet pastry shop. Came in for the cream puffs we saw online and left with a mango sticky rice and black sesame version. We also couldn't refuse the adorable raspberry lychee tart. As a huge sesame fan, the black sesame was very subtle but also a little confusing as to the taste vibe they were going for. The raspberry lychee tart had the softest macarons on top and the flavor was subtle but sweet. The star was definitely the mango sticky rice version!! That was an explosion of everything that is right in the world!! Just do it!! Definitely worth a stop on your nyc adventures.

For $5 for a big cream puff with a wonderfully, pleasant, fragrant earl grey cold cream, it's a well executed dessert. There's no where to sit, but good value for the size. Be prepared to finish once bitten.

If you have been lucky enough to visit Gosh... You have peaked, you reached climax. If you haven't... What are you waiting for!

I loved every single night I've spent at this swanky lounge. Exploring the different floors, trying different cocktails (there's one called 'Sadomaso', which I can't get out of my head!), and running into cool, edgy downtown crowd.

Gosh is amazing, though the team likes to say "Gosh is Good". This place feels more like a cult than a bar, and I will gladly sign up to be a part of it!
Great place with great people!!

the girl at the door is the most fascinating yet intimidating woman i’ve ever seen. 10/10 place, highly recommend.
