review_text: Cozy and casual dining place with interesting fusion dishes of European & Japanese styles. Different entry site than the Michelin star restaurant l’abeille but food tasted good and fresh!

The restaurant was on our try list and the overall experience was very enjoyable. The service staff - knowledgeable and very attentive - loved that part! The ambience - beautiful, I liked the white marble filigree section over the Sheesh mahal part. The drinks were good, the mango pinacolada was not as comforting as a mango lassi is. The food portions are generous and enjoyable. The butter chicken experience was ok, the traditional butter chicken was a crowd favorite when compared to the other 2. The daal musaafar was buttery goodness, cinnamon forward but unfortunately overly salty!! The panner was fresh and well seasoned. The coconut subji - unique and very tasty. The chat was yum but again was not a stand out dish. The other dishes were ok as well but nothing to write home and it was all very pricey! The ras malai was very yum! Overall good, but not a repeat place!

Nice decor, decent food... the service could be better. We had the Black Daal and the Baingan Bharta with lachha paratha. The Daal was good but the Bharta was outstanding. A bit pricey but good food. The only feedback I have is about the service - the older gentleman taking our order was a bit curt and not exactly very friendly. It's the little things that can make or break a dining experience.

Food was below average woth unbalanced flavors and use of stale ingredients . Service subpar especially when 20% gratuity is charged upfront. For fine dining establishment this place is disappointing.
Great experience and service

Must visit for its vibe. Exceptional indian cuisine served as a fusion and amazing cocktails.
Super expensive though.

I stayed here for 3 weeks for a work trip and loved it. The rooms are very clean, nice views, staff were all super nice and attentive. It was my first time in NY so don’t have another hotel to compare it to but coming from London i loved it! Did not find the rooms too small and the location is really fantastic. Thank you!

Really bad service

Amazing location in SoHo and great management team
Rose Jasmine tea was good would come again. If tea flavor was slightly stronger, would be 5*.

The bubble tea here was amazing, and the atmosphere was absolutely wonderful! Ethan, Leo, and Ben provided incredible service and helped create such a welcoming and enjoyable experience. The drinks were delicious, perfectly priced, and I truly enjoyed every sip. I’ll definitely be coming back!

The workers here are very efficient and super casual to make small talk with. Plus their drinks taste very authentic, very similar to the kind of tea base used in China’s boba stores. Definitely coming back in the future to try more of their menu!

Ethan, leo, and Ben were very helpful when ordering drinks

Initially just wanted to try the food and I didn’t regret it! Food was excellent and the service provided was excellent and a special thanks to Sagar for being so kind and helpful! Great job 👏 and great food too!

Good, authentic Indian food and a great atmosphere!

- The Shammi kebabs were absolutely amazing.
- Chicken Kaali mirchi was right to our taste , must try. Get it with a rumali roti , it was super good.

- We ended our meal with jalebi, which wasn’t too sweet. Loved it!

I would recommend to go for small plates more as they are better

The hosts were great and welcoming, and we loved the ambience. It’s a little bit expensive, but still feels worth it!

A fantastic find.
The best coffee in the neighborhood.

Cute little cafeeee

What a beautiful cafe!

They also have a really interesting tea selection as well. The matcha with house-made blackberry is unlike anything I have ever tasted, they work so well together! The best part: we enjoyed it while listening to records on an actual record player!
A great experience…

Ordered for delivery and the food was very good. The bossam was the favorite. The cod omelet was also good and I got the cod spaghetti but I didnt love it I wish you could sub udon noodles. Delivery was pretty fast and would order again.

The boy server was so kind. Nicest service I've gotten in nyc. Will definitely return back!!
Hands down some of the best Korean fried chicken I've had! The seasoned chicken was amazing, and the restaurant interior is very clean and welcoming. Definitely coming back!
Hosted a large work dinner here. It was a great experience, great food, and Oscar was very excited and welcoming.

I never, ever write reviews but Oscar's exceptional kindness and hospitality, the restaurant's cozy ambiance, and the remarkable flavors of the creative, yet refined menu made my entire night. My best friend and I have very busy schedules, so whenever we get together, it's such a special occasion full of stories, updates, and lots of love, and Bowery Bungalow was the perfect space to enjoy each other's company over an unforgettable meal. I will absolutely recommend this gem of a restaurant to my friends and family, and basically anyone I love (especially recommend the amazingly tender lamb, the fresh and bright Lebanese salad, and the beautifully balanced cocktails)! ❤️ Thank you for making our night even more magical :)

What a great find! We tried this place tonight on a whim and couldn’t believe how good it was! The place is beautiful and unique, and immediately makes you feel like you’re somewhere special. Then the host, Oscar, and the lovely waitstaff make you feel like you’re the most important guests of the evening. Next comes the delicious cocktails. I had The One With Rum, and my friend had the bourbon cocktail. Both were exquisite. But then the food came, and oh my goodness! The Spicy Lamb Toast was mind-blowing. The pork belly Shishkatori almost made me cry with how delicious and unique it was. And then the mains! The Braised Lamb and Pan Seared Branzino were among the most innovative and perfectly executed dishes I’ve eaten in years. Between the delicious food, the personalized and warm service, and the lovely decor, I can’t believe my good fortune in finding this place before it becomes too hot to get a reservation. It’ll be a favorite for date nights and group dinners for sure.

I’ve always entertained my friends visiting the city in La Mercerie for the ambiance and food (and always bought a thing or two from The Guild), however my most recent was extremely disappointing. I understood the lunch menu was switching so we tried to place our orders ASAP, but most of the items we wanted were already gone — it took a lot of time for the server to tell us that the items are unavailable from the time the order was taken. Food took forever to come out, and I felt like we were not taken cared of and the service just felt really short and horrible. It already took time to get our orders and even longer for the food to be served, and I noticed that other people seated way AFTER us were served first. I had to ask TWICE (with a long time of waiting in between). It’s not like we had a huge group order too. Other guests were looked after more, and I felt we were racially discriminated because they obviously preferred and paid more attention to a certain group of people. Mind you, I live in New York so I can always tell the subtleties and difference in service. I did not want to ruin my friends’ experience by making a fuss. This is so disappointing because I always recommended this spot. Wouldn’t be back anytime

The music was perfect too and really added to the whole atmosphere. It just fits the place.

Consumers should look beyond the credit limit they are offered. Read the terms, understand the APR, calculate the long-term cost, and determine how much of every payment may actually reduce principal.

Corporate responsibility should not end when credit is issued. It should include transparency about what that credit can ultimately cost the consumer. Based on my experience, if I could leave ZERO STARS, I would.

Café Fig — A Wonderful New Addition to SoHo!

What a wonderful little café that recently opened on the corner of Broome and Mott! Café Fig brings something special to the neighborhood with its Greek-inspired coffee and creative beverages.

The owner, George, is an awesome, laid-back guy who makes you feel right at home.

I ordered the Freddo Cappuccino and the Banana Churro, and both were fantastic.

The Freddo Cappuccino was done exactly how I'd imagine a proper Greek-style coffee should be, with that beautiful, creamy foam and a little touch of honey. Excellent!

The Banana Churro was such a treat! Light, flavorful, and surprisingly refreshing, with a unique banana milk flavor. Almost like having dessert in a cup without being overly heavy or sweet. Definitely one of the more interesting drinks I've had recently.

Beyond the drinks, I really appreciate the attention to detail throughout the café. It's cute, quaint, and thoughtfully designed. The rich maroon interior, inspired by the color of a fig, gives the space a warm and distinctive personality. You can tell a lot of intention went into creating it.

And as a bonus, it's right next to a great bánh mì spot! Grab your morning or afternoon coffee at Café Fig, then finish the day with a delicious bánh mì next door. Not a bad combination!

Definitely recommend stopping by and saying hi to George. It's exciting to have another independent café in the neighborhood, especially one that's doing Greek coffee right. Welcome to SoHo, Café Fig!

Eat Offbeat operates the cafe area and is an NYC-based organization that employs refugees and immigrants to celebrate and elevate the craft & artisanship of cooking from around the world. the cafe space feels like an art gallery--adorned with art and art-centric books, somewhat intimate seating, and bright art lighting positioned above. the ambiance evokes upscale with the touch of minimalism in the bare white walls but is welcoming in its curated cafe menu of coffees, teas, juices, and small bites. it's clear that the decor and vibe are to evoke creativity and thought as you enjoy a coffee or a bite. very much place to share, but also to protect its ethos of spirit. been here several times — enjoyed a cortado and Americano to-go. both were made proficiently. currently, the cafe uses a South American (maybe El Salvadoran?) medium roast coffee that has a pleasant deep nuttiness and a mildly sweet undertones  as a coffee. very much a smooth caffeine for the winter times. the last time i stopped here, ordered a Turkish coffee and enjoyed it at the cafe. not sure the “Turkish coffee” is actually traditional coffee from Turkey, but the coffee served in a Turkish style. it's served on a small silver tray where a "cezve" (the handled counter where the coffee is boiled),  fincan (the small 2 oz. cup) for slowly sipping the coffee, and a Syrian Barazak Cookie (there are two choices of sweets). it's very much an aesthetically pleasing presentation. the coffee is served hot as it foams up...the coffee tastes richer and thicker because it is served this way. it's fancy in a nonchalant way. Turkish coffee is meant to be enjoyed in a social way, so bring a friend! the service at Eat OffBeat is pleasant and hospitable. the barista is conscientious in the coffee-making and service. the patrons of the Atelier and the cafe  from my experience are from the arts world, but aren't pretentious or snooty which is refreshing. it is a nice respite from the hustle and bustle of the city and the hustle and bustle of tooo many coffee shops. take a breath here and enjoy art aka life.

First, it seems only one person was serving the entire restaurant. And while I won't get into details about the actual service, suffice it to say it was about as good as the akra appetizer we ordered.

So, we placed our order: two apps and two entrees. We both stuck to water. My cousin ordered a cranberry juice (more on this later) but they had none that evening. Not only did the apps take forever to reach our table, there was maybe a 20 minute gap between the 1st and 2nd app. The akra, while beautiful, was bland. And the pikliz (more on this later) didn't elevate the taste. We also ordered wings with a spicy mango sauce. The sauce tasted more like a splashed on afterthought than an integrated element. Again, it wasn't terrible, but it wasn't memorable.

Let's move on to the entrees: goat and griot. Thought was definitely put into the presentation and both proteins were tender as a muh. So tender they made our mouths water. So, you can't imagine our disappointment when we dug into our plates. Everything tasted like a shadow of the flavors that raised us. The side of pikliz (seriously, wait till I tell tale) didn't help, accentuate or elevate the dish--it was just added heat. And, quick side note: we added one side after we got our entrees, which...never made it to the table.

Oh, and someone was celebrating a birthday that night. A fact the DJ refused to let us forget. Have I been living under a rock? I had no idea there were so many genres and versions of Happy Birthday. And he must have played all of them at a volume OSHA would fine for such a small space.

We finish our food and get our check--and not because we ordered the check. We weren't asked if we wanted dessert, which I did. Being as greedy as I am, I had my eye on the pain patat. But without prompting from our table we get a check.

The cranberry juice they didn't have? It was on the check. The side we ordered that never made it to our table? It was on the check. To add insult to injury, they charged separately for the pikliz. THE PIKLIZ?! But what really and truly blackened my djon djon was the automatic gratuity. Now, I just reviewed the menu to make sure. Nowhere inside or outside the restaurant (that I can remember) or on the menu was an advisory about automatic gratuity. I've eaten at restaurants that add automatic gratuity, but usually not for a table of 2 and always with obvious signage.

★★★★★ | One of the best dining experiences we’ve had in NYC

Noury is exactly the kind of restaurant New York needs more of. Thoughtful, inventive cooking, beautiful ingredients, an excellent wine selection, and genuinely warm hospitality. Every dish felt intentional without being overly complicated or precious. The Japanese influences are beautifully executed, and the entire meal struck that rare balance between sophisticated and completely unpretentious.

From the incredibly fresh sashimi and beautifully composed small plates to the crispy kakiage, everything was exceptional. Even the simplest dishes were memorable, and the melon dessert was the perfect ending.

A special shoutout to Kim, who took care of us throughout the evening and guided us through the wines. She was absolutely wonderful. Knowledgeable, intuitive, attentive without ever hovering, and genuinely passionate about what she was serving. Her wine recommendations were fantastic, and she made the entire evening feel personal and effortless. That kind of hospitality is increasingly rare in New York, and Kim deserves real recognition for it.

What I particularly loved about Noury is that nothing feels forced. The food speaks for itself, the room is intimate and inviting, and the service makes you want to linger over another glass of wine.

Five stars, without hesitation. A restaurant we’ll absolutely be returning to, and one I’m almost reluctant to tell too many people about. Thank you, Kim, and the entire Noury team, for such a wonderful evening.

It seems like hot, humid food was packaged in a sealed container without proper cooling, creating the perfect environment for mold to grow overnight. I ended up having to throw the entire box into the trash.

an art cafe hidden in plain sight of Atelier Jolie, an arts collective / cultural center in NoHo, which was opened by Angelina Jolie. those in the arts scene might recognize the address as it was occupied by Andy Warhol and Jean-Michael Basquiat a long time ago...and it’s formerly the home of the speak-easy-ish restaurant Bohemian. Eat Offbeat operates the cafe area and is an NYC-based organization that employs refugees and immigrants to celebrate and elevate the craft & artisanship of cooking from around the world. the cafe space feels like an art gallery--adorned with art and art-centric books, somewhat intimate seating, and bright art lighting positioned above. the ambiance evokes upscale with the touch of minimalism in the bare white walls but is welcoming in its curated cafe menu of coffees, teas, juices, and small bites. it's clear that the decor and vibe are to evoke creativity and thought as you enjoy a coffee or a bite. very much place to share, but also to protect its ethos of spirit. been here several times — enjoyed a cortado and Americano to-go. both were made proficiently. currently, the cafe uses a South American (maybe El Salvadoran?) medium roast coffee that has a pleasant deep nuttiness and a mildly sweet undertones  as a coffee. very much a smooth caffeine for the winter times. the last time i stopped here, ordered a Turkish coffee and enjoyed it at the cafe. not sure the “Turkish coffee” is actually traditional coffee from Turkey, but the coffee served in a Turkish style. it's served on a small silver tray where a "cezve" (the handled counter where the coffee is boiled),  fincan (the small 2 oz. cup) for slowly sipping the coffee, and a Syrian Barazak Cookie (there are two choices of sweets). it's very much an aesthetically pleasing presentation. the coffee is served hot as it foams up...the coffee tastes richer and thicker because it is served this way. it's fancy in a nonchalant way. Turkish coffee is meant to be enjoyed in a social way, so bring a friend! the service at Eat OffBeat is pleasant and hospitable. the barista is conscientious in the coffee-making and service. the patrons of the Atelier and the cafe  from my experience are from the arts world, but aren't pretentious or snooty which is refreshing. it is a nice respite from the hustle and bustle of the city and the hustle and bustle of tooo many coffee shops. take a breath here and enjoy art aka life.

Honestly, I’m extremely frustrated with this experience. I live uptown, so coming downtown to this restaurant is a trip for me, and I specifically came because I’ve been dying to try one of their menu items.

I arrived shortly after 12 PM, and the gates were still down. The open sign wasn’t on, and there was nothing on the door explaining why they were closed. I called, no answer. I even waited until after 1 PM and came back, and they were STILL closed.

I completely understand that things happen. Maybe it was a personal matter, staffing issue, emergency, or something else entirely.

But the problem is that there was absolutely no communication. Nothing on the door, nothing on Instagram, nothing on the ordering site explaining the closure or saying when they planned to open.

This is now the second time I’ve made the trip specifically to come here, and both times they’ve been closed. At this point, how am I supposed to trust the posted hours or feel confident making the trip downtown if I can’t rely on the business to actually be open during those hours?

If your hours say you’re open at 12 PM, customers should reasonably be able to expect you to be open at 12 PM.

If that’s not possible, then please update your hours or communicate with your customers. I genuinely wanted to try this place, which is why I kept trying, but this experience has been incredibly irritating and disappointing.

We had a wonderful experience at KALYE, a Filipino restaurant in New York that I highly recommend. We enjoyed traditional dishes served on banana leaves, which added a special touch to our meal. At KALYE, you have the option to eat with your hands or use clear plastic gloves—both ways are enjoyable!

The owner, Mr. Rob Mallari-D'Auria, was very engaging and made a point to visit each table to inquire about our experience and introduce himself. When he came to our table, we had the joy of sharing our Filipino heritage with him. My brother mentioned that we were born in the Philippines, which led to lots of laughter as we switched from English to Tagalog—except for my son, who was born here and hasn't learned Tagalog or our dialect, Pangalatok.

Mr. Rob was generous and offered us a complimentary shot, which was delightful, along with an amazing Ube Mocktail! I can't recommend the Ube sliders enough; they are a must-try for anyone planning to visit.

review_text: The hotel was conveniently located and aesthetics were nice. Some exceptional design qualities within the room and I appreciated that the window actually opened. The mattress location was wonderful as was the view but the mattress itself was an old spring mattress with no topper or anything to make it even a little comfy. The pillows were all bulky and firm and there was nothing cloud-like or comfy about sleeping here for two night. We woke up feeling achy and irritated from a rough night sleep. The bench seating was also poorly cushioned to the point I sat in a throw pillow to drink my coffee and put my makeup on. Breakfast and coffee shop was great. Excellent cortado and smoked salmon toast. We also tried the Jammie eggs (just ok) and the mushroom egg sandwich (nice to look at but not tasty) as well as some cookies and breakfast breads. We booked through platinum and were guaranteed late check out. We checked out before 1:00 for which they charged us $200 which will now have to be dealt with by Amex. We found all staff aside from front desk to be super fun and friendly. Never ventured up to the rooftop this time, unfortunately but plan to stay here again once they handle their mattress situation.

review_text:
My stay at PUBLIC Hotel left a lot to be desired, starting with a frustrating check-in experience. Despite arriving at 3:10 PM (past the 3:00 PM check-in time), I was unable to use the iPad check-in because I hadn't received a room number yet.

When I spoke to the front desk, I was told my room wasn’t ready because the previous guest had a late check-out, and that my personal request for robes and slippers—which I had submitted three weeks in advance—was causing an additional delay.

When I asked for an ETA, I was simply told to come back in 20 minutes. I returned around 3:30pm and spoke with another staff member who gave a vague answer. Given the inconvenient delay that nearly made me late for an uptown reservation at 5pm, I asked if a late check-out could be accommodated for my departure day. I was told they couldn't approve it at the desk and I’d have to call down later. No gesture or accommodation was offered to alleviate the inconvenience, making for a poor first impression.

To top it off, when I finally got to the room, the robes and slippers I requested three weeks prior were missing. When I asked about them later that evening, I was told they were completely out of slippers, though we did eventually receive the robes.

On a positive note, the room itself was clean. However, noise traveled easily through the door and you could hear people talking in the hall, making it less than peaceful.

Ultimately, I’ve had much better service and hospitality at other New York City hotels, and unfortunately, I will not be returning.

review_text:
This is a really shiny hotel that you might be better off staying away from.

Travel + Leisure said this was a cool hotel. Okay.

I tried to book online. I got a confirmation screen, but no email or card charge notification, so I tried again after 10 mins (do not do this, it was dumb of me). Got a second confirmation screen, but again, no email or card charge. Tried to call twice, but couldn't get through to a real person, so I guess I'll have to go there.

I'm there. Yep, there are two reservations under my name! Luckily the person at the front desk was very kind and canceled one for me. To their credit, everyone at Public was very nice and tried to be helpful.

I check into my room; it was very cold and I'd booked this hotel specifically to get a bath. I try the bath; the knob is weird and the spigot won't work. Call the front desk; they're sending an engineer. Harris, the engineer, was very nice. Bathtub is broken, they move me to another room after a half-hour.

In that room, there's no hot water. Even if the bath wasn't an issue, taking a shower with the way the water currently was would have been really unpleasant. Call the front desk, they're gonna send the engineer again.

At this point I have to leave for an event. While I'm out, the hotel texts to say the water is okay now. Cool.

When I get back, the water really is fixed and I get to take the bath. I eat dinner, and when I go to put my food away at midnight in the fridge at midnight, I realize the fridge was left open (not by me) and it's actually warm. I.. just get mad and throw my stuff away.

At 2 am, the fire alarm goes off. I'm on Floor 10. I head towards Stair A. Once I hit Floor 3, thank goodness, the alarm stops. I want to get out of the stairs and take the elevator back up. Well, this hotel has several floors that are not numbered--they're called things like LL, G, L, and some of the doors say they exit to the street, and some don't, and what's creepier is that when you get to the door you think will let you out, there's another door beyond it in a hallway that's completely unmarked, and you get scared when you're completely shit-for-brains tired and scared at 2 am that you'll go through one door, get locked out of the stairs, but then won't know where you are when you go through the second door and won't be able to get back. After a few scary tries, I made it back to the lobby, which is LL and not L I guess.. I can't remember now.

Anyways, in the morning, after two hours of horrible sleep, I cried. I told the manager, Kelvin, all of this. I will never go back to this hotel, and I do not think I should've had to pay for this stay.

I've been sitting on this experience for almost two months and just can't shake it ... so I feel compelled to write this negative review. On Sunday, June 7th around 4PM, I received what was likely the worst customer service at any restaurant or bar I have ever been to from the bartended with the red hair/beard. Just look at the incoherent reply to this review and you get all the information you need about this place. Pointing to the outside weather as the reason they are serving WARM drinks???? I, honestly, wouldn't feel comfortable drinking a beverage or eating food prepared by someone this incompetent. Good luck to anyone who goes here.

To set the scene, I had spent literally all day walking around Brooklyn in the sun and heat completing a scavenger hunt. I was hot and sweaty and just wanted to sit and have a chat with a friend over a refreshing, cold beverage. Literally all I could imagine en route to Black Crescent was a crisp, ice-cold Diet Coke. Of all the things I could have ordered, a Diet Coke is just about the simplest thing you can order at a bar. Not too much to ask for, right? Well, apparently it was. And for the record, my friend ordered alcoholic drinks and we ordered food ... didn't just come here for a soda. When I ordered my Diet Coke, what I got was something resembling brown water that tasted extremely watered down. So, I got up (didn't wave the bartender over) and politely told him the drink tasted really watered down. I can still see the look of annoyance he gave me clearly in my mind. I went back to my friend at our table. A few moments later, the bartender came out with a glass of ice and a glass of diet coke and plopped both on the table with an undeniably shitty attitude. Despite my treatment, I still remained polite, even though he was showing me less than no respect. With the components now separated for me to combine, it became clear what the problem was. The glass of Diet Coke wasn't just room temperature ... it was WARM. So, what had clearly happened was there were bottles of soft drinks being stored in the warm back room and being poured over ice and presented to customers as an appropriate drink. It isn't.

Not to spare words but how does that bartender still have a job? How lazy do you need to be to get annoyed at someone ordering a soft drink and then give them attitude when they are communicating a valid issue to you? I will never be coming back here. This bartender is mentioned in multiple negative reviews over the years but I guess the establishment just doesn't care. And one more thing. There's a special place in the afterlife for watering holes that serve soft drinks out of tiny cocktail glasses. Like, really? How is this place still in business?

Fiat Café is the kind of relaxed neighborhood restaurant that works well when you want a satisfying Italian meal without the formality or prices of an upscale restaurant. It’s on Mott Street in Nolita, within easy walking distance of both SoHo and Little Italy, but removed from the most crowded blocks. The outdoor seating is especially enjoyable for people-watching and taking in the energy of the neighborhood.

We ordered quite a spread: the Misto Cheese and Cold Cuts, Fried Calamari, Steamed Mussels, Polenta with Italian Fennel Sausage, Creamy Chicken Tagliatelle in Pink Sauce, and NY Strip Steak with Chimichurri, along with a bottle of Chardonnay. The calamari takes about 15 minutes because it is cooked to order, and it arrived tasting freshly fried rather than pre-cooked and reheated. Everything else was fresh and solid as well. The food isn’t exceptional or especially refined, but it’s satisfying, fairly priced, and supported by an extensive menu with plenty to choose from.

Our server, Alex, made the experience particularly enjoyable. She was warm, accommodating, attentive, and genuinely pleasant to talk to without ever making the service feel intrusive. Combined with the quick service and lively location, Fiat Café is a dependable, welcoming neighborhood spot that offers very good value for the area.

Extremely disappointing and disrespectful experience. I will not be returning ever again. They scam you if you’re paying with $50 bills or $100 in cash.

From the moment my friends and I arrived, the male bartender with locs and a mustache serving us had an unnecessary attitude toward me. We understood that the bar was busy, so we initially gave him the benefit of the doubt and assumed he might simply be having a bad day.

I ordered a $17 drink and a $12 appetizer and paid with a $50 bill. He gave me only 44 cents and did not give me a receipt. I was confused because the change was clearly incorrect, so when he saw my visible confusion he asked, “What’s wrong?” I calmly and politely told him, “The change is incorrect. I gave you a $50 bill.”

Instead of explaining the transaction or correcting the change, he simply printed a receipt, slapped it down on the bar, and walked away. The receipt showed that I had supposedly given him $32, even though I had given him $50. Based on the total, he should have given me significantly more change. I was not rude, confrontational, or belligerent. I simply pointed out that the amount was wrong. I chose not to argue because I was not going to let the situation ruin my night and he was clearly not going to correct his error.

Unfortunately, his behavior only became worse.

My appetizer took well over 15–20 minutes to arrive. Since my group of friends and I were ready to leave, I politely asked for the appetizer could be cancelled because it still had not arrived and to get a refund. He immediately shook his head and said, “No, it’s already being made,” and slightly chuckled in an extremely dismissive manner. I understand that an order may already be in preparation, but he could have been professional. His response left my girl friend shocked as well.

What was especially disturbing was that his disrespect toward me noticeably escalated after my guy friend left to step outside . My girlfriend even asked whether something was wrong because she noticed the change in his demeanor. We had been patient and understanding because the bar was busy, yet he continued treating me as though I had personally offended him, even though I had done nothing to him. Yet other customers weren’t receiving this treatment we were getting from him.

The girl working directly beside him witnessed the interaction and never checked in. While we were dealing with the situation, a server eventually brought the appetizer. I apologized to him and asked him to give it to someone else and let them know it was on the house because I no longer wanted it and did not want the situation to escalate further.

When my male friend returned inside to understand what had happened, the bartender’s demeanor suddenly changed. He was much more pleasant toward my friend and even gave him an inaccurate version of events, including claiming that he had offered to package the food for me to take home. That was never offered to me. Two of our other friends witnessed the interaction and noticed the clear difference in how he treated me compared with how he treated my male friend.

I have worked in hospitality management for over 15 years, so I understand busy restaurants, kitchen delays, difficult customers, and orders that may already be in preparation. None of that excuses dismissive or hostile customer service.

This was not about the $12 appetizer. It was not even about the incorrect change from the $50 bill. It was about being treated with unnecessary disrespect after calmly pointing out that I had not received the correct change, then being dismissed when I asked to cancel an appetizer that had not arrived, followed by an obvious change in demeanor once a guy customer became involved.

I left feeling disrespected, dismissed, and singled out. I came in intending to enjoy myself and spend money at the establishment. Instead, I had to repeatedly defend why I deserved basic courtesy.

There are too many places in NYC where I can spend my money and receive professional, respectful service. I will not be returning to Pretty Ricky’s.

What bothered me most was that as I was leaving, I could hear that same employee talking to his coworkers about me ordering the espresso and making snarky comments about it. At that point, it went beyond an awkward interaction and felt unnecessarily disrespectful.

As someone who grew up in China, I honestly don’t have very high expectations for Chinese restaurants in NYC. They almost always feel commercial to me—but not necessarily “commercially” good, even when they have excellent reviews.

We were strolling around SoHo and chose this place for dinner almost randomly. Even before walking in, I saw two large groups of non-Chinese diners waiting by the entrance and thought to myself, another place that’s probably just going to be OK.

I couldn’t have been more wrong.

Except for the fact that the staff members we encountered spoke fluent English, everything else somehow felt so… Chinese.

The service was friendly in exactly the right amount. No one kept coming over to ask, as a formality, whether “everything was good.” At one point, I switched one dish for another, half “admitting” that I wanted to learn some tricks from that particular dish, and the waitress simply gave me this genuine, understanding smile.

Later, all of our dishes had arrived except one, and we weren’t quite sure whether it had actually been included in our order. When we asked another waitress, she immediately understood what we meant and responded in such a calm, reassuring way—without treating the question as if we were pushing her to hurry up with the dish.

There’s a nuanced difference there, if you know what I mean.

The food also came out unexpectedly fast, and the flavors were spot-on. That, of course, is the biggest reason I came away thinking: this place is authentic.

And then there was the space itself.

When we were first seated, I felt lucky that the two of us had been given a four-person table. But once I sat down and looked around, I realized they simply weren’t “stingy” with their seating arrangements. That kind of generosity with space is not particularly common in NYC restaurants.

At first, I also thought the room was a little noisy and perhaps not very conducive to a deep conversation. Half an hour later, though, we found ourselves talking about our feelings toward different family members. Somehow, the ambience was just right: enough life and noise around us that you could let some emotion out, without the room becoming so quiet that you suddenly felt exposed and responsible for filling every silence.

When we walked out, I said to myself, I really need to leave a positive review for this team.

So I took one last picture before we left.

I decided to visit this place because of its great reviews and convenient location, but unfortunately, I experienced extremely rude and unprofessional service from a female staff member wearing a hat and glasses.

Before ordering, I simply asked, “Where is the restroom?” She responded very aggressively, “ONLY CUSTOMERS!”

I explained, “Oh, I am a customer! I just wanted to use the restroom before placing my order.” However, she gave me directions in an extremely unfriendly manner. While I was waiting, she also rudely told me to move out of the way three separate times.

I initially let it go, thinking perhaps she was treating me that way because I hadn’t placed my order yet.

But when I came back to order, all she said was “NO SEAT.” No explanation, no courtesy, just those two words.

Throughout my trip, I’ve had such wonderful experiences thanks to the warmth and kindness of New Yorkers. This was the first time I encountered someone so unnecessarily rude.

I don’t think she realizes that, for international visitors, a single interaction like this can shape their impression of an entire city or even a country.

If you’re too tired or unwilling to provide basic customer service, perhaps you should reconsider working in the service industry. Being tired is understandable, but it doesn’t justify treating customers disrespectfully.

Considering this establishment’s reputation and popularity, I was genuinely shocked by the level of service. In fact, this experience was so disappointing that I’m leaving a Google review for the very first time.

This was the one and only truly unpleasant experience during my otherwise warm, wonderful, and precious trip to New York.

I sincerely hope the management takes this feedback seriously and uses it as an opportunity to improve how customers are treated.

Please don’t dismiss customer feedback simply because your establishment is popular. Popularity should never be an excuse for poor service. I hope you accept this criticism with humility and take it seriously rather than ignoring it.

The Melancholy of the Reheated: Pomme Frites Loses its Mojo
There is an alchemy to the humble frites of Belgium, a crisp, golden outer shell yielding to a pillowy, steaming interior, forged through the sacred ritual of the double-fry. For years, the East Village sanctuary known as Pomme Frites was New York’s improbable temple to this art. To walk into the original postage-stamp storefront on Second Avenue was to inhale a heady, unapologetic cloud of beef tallow and anticipation. They were freshly cut, meticulously crafted, and utterly transcendent.
The resurrection of Pomme Frites in the neighborhood should have been a culinary triumph. Instead, it is a sobering exercise in nostalgia unfulfilled.
The fries arriving at the table today bear no resemblance to their exalted predecessor. Gone is the earthy, irregular charm of the freshly butchered potato. In their place are glorifed diner fries- uniform, industrialized, and unmistakably frozen. They possess the hollow, cardboard crunch of mass production, lacking both structural integrity and soul. They are the sort of side dish one apathetically pushes to the side of a mediocre bistro plate, a ghost of a recipe processed for convenience rather than reverence.
The kitchen’s distraction appears entirely diverted toward camouflage. The venue leans heavily on an overkill of gimmicky sauces—dozens of flavoredmayos and artisanal drizzles that arrive like a colorful defense mechanism. It is a cynical sleight of hand: if you bury a mediocre starch under truffle-garlic aioli and mango chutney, does anyone notice the tragedy beneath?
If even a fraction of the energy expended on curating an endless wall of condiments had been invested in the actual potato; in sourcing, cutting, and executing a proper made-to-order fry, there might have been a product worth cheering for. As it stands, the soul has unceremoniously departed the premises, leaving behind only a branded shell. Two stars, awarded purely out of respect for the sheer effort of keeping the lights on.

This is one of those places, I would say, where you don’t go out of your way to come here but definitely worth stopping by if in the area for work or school. Has outdoor seating but is very much a grab and go place.

Apps were the best part of the menu. Empanadas, octupus and tuna were excellent. Entrees were less impressive. Would go back but would stick to apps next time.

Came here to celebrate my birthday. Nice atmosphere and good food but terrible service, which effects the overall experience. When I asked the server a question about the menu instead of responding to me about my question, they looked at and responsed to my friend. Unbelievable, blatant racism. The food had great flavor, the service was attentive, and the place had a warm, relaxed feel without being too formal. It’s the kind of restaurant that feels good for a date night, dinner with friends, or just trying something a little different.
It's good, all good, but not great. And it's a bit more expensive than what you'd expect.

One of my favorite places in NYC, a true home away from home. The loveliest staff, a great selection of games for all group sizes that they can recommend to you if you need help, actually good coffee, a robust beer (and cider!) selection, and always good vibes.
Stopped by while visiting, had a great time ripping some magic packs and playing games with a kind stranger. The atmosphere in the cafe was cozy and welcoming. Their board game selection was massive.

We stopped here during our first ever trip to NYC (for my husbands birthday). I searched game stores and this was highly rated, and deservedly so. We like to look for unique games or locally created. The staff were enthusiastic and extremely helpful. They offered great options but unfortunately we were limited due to luggage size. We walked out with a few treasures and a definite stop on our next trip.

First time in NYC and The Uncommon was our second game store. Staff was fantastic! Gave great recommendations on local boardgames as well as a couple unique choices based on the conversation my wife had with the employee. We were so excited, we forgot tontake pics of it. Great, easy-going experience and had a wonderful visit! Thank you!!!
This was amazing! A brilliant selection of games, with a knowledgeable staff who got us the perfect games to match all our whimsical requests! We even got a free iced coffee :)) will defo be back!!
Love the pastrami sendwitch.
This place is so overhyped. There's a long queue for dinner and the sandwich isn't even that good?
The pastrami and the beef were incredible. Don't lose your ticket when you enter, whether you order anything or not.

After waiting in line for a very long time, we were met with a rude and disrespectful attitude from the staff at the door. The inside was incredibly noisy, and the staff's general approach was cold. Tipping felt almost mandatory—you constantly feel pressured.

As for the food, the taste definitely doesn't live up to the hype. We ordered a Reuben and a Pastrami sandwich, but couldn't finish either of them. The sandwich was very hard to eat because of the bread, and we didn't like the taste of the spread on it at all.

Rather than a restaurant environment where you can enjoy yourself and spend time, it has a complete fast-food atmosphere with an 'eat and get out quickly' concept. I don't think I'll be choosing this place again
Great wine pairings from female owned wineries. Staff was excellent and accommodating. Great value for a multi course, vegetarian high end meal!

Obviously the food is amazing, no doubt about that. We loved every dish and every single wine pairing - we caught the last night of the summer menu and are so glad we did. But particularly, our server Clinton and the manager (did not catch her name) made the night fun and stress-free, and were so kind when forgot to disclose an allergy. When I couldn’t eat one of the courses, they brought a second serving of my favorite previous course so I wouldn’t have any less food. We will be back for sure!

My sister gave me a hefty milestone birthday gift certificate that covered a portion of our bill. The food tasting menu and wine were all delicious. Love trying different vegan restaurants and although this was one of the more upscale dining places, it was really excellent.

Los 7 tiempos del menú estuvieron muy ricos. Sabores y texturas originales y ricos. La opción de maridaje con vino sin alcohol es muy original y estuvieron muy ricos.
El servicio fue algo lento, pero, el lugar nos gustó por la atmósfera tranquila para poder platicar y disfrutar los alimentos.
I tried the banana pudding that a friend of a friend purchased from this place. Hands down the BEST EVER.

Sabrina was very professional from the consultation to the execution of everything was very smooth. The ladies that asist her are very kind also. Everyone was very happy and pleased with how everything came out and how delicious it was especially my daughter. You made her birthday very special ❤️
Definitely the best banana pudding in town. And Peggy was very sweet and wonderful.

I have to start by saying that chatgpt is the one that recommended this restaurant to me after I told it what I loved. I was presently surprised. Everything was perfection. The wood ear mushrooms were prepared with the perfect amount of 'crisp' preserved. And the dressing had the perfect amount of strong bite. But nothing overpowering. You will not even have to drink water.
Their cocktails are prepared very well. Not sweet. Have you ever had buttery pork that melts in your mouth? You will have it here.
I provided pictures to the dishes. But I literally ordered by showing them pictures from previous Google reviews, so I apologize if I do not provide the names. But I truly hope I can make it back here again one day.
The food was outstanding. We ordered the specialties: the half-Peking duck; the cold sesame noodles; the orange beef. We left feeling stuffed but very satisfied.

Listen. Most of the food was subpar, it lacked salt and spice. Baffling. Truly, a disappointment.

The duck was nice and crispy, and they offered plenty of crepes along with it. However, the sauce with the duck didn't really taste like much.

The service was fine, they were attentive, if not a little disgruntled with us. The drinks were good, if not a little sparse on the alcohol content.

Overall, I wouldn't recommend this spot to anyone looking for a dinner in Chinatown.

Great donuts, the old fashioned are a MUST as they’re better than the regular raised. I've been going here for about 2 years or so..their taro drink is the best taro I've had so far especially in the area. It's to the point that everyone around me knows this place because I speak so much about it.

We split the Focaccia & Ricotta, Montauk Tile Fish Tartar, Tuscan Kale, Tonnarelli Cacio e Pepe pasta, Bucatini Pesto pasta, and Spicy Sopresseta pizza. Yum. Left stuffed and satisfied.

I loved it! I'd never had a sushi experience like that before, and it was absolutely incredible. It was one of my favorite things about my trip to New York. I thought it was great that you don't have to leave a tip and that they serve you water without you having to order a drink. The beer was delicious and reasonably priced.
We went tor their omakase on a Sunday afternoon. We thoroughly enjoyed our meal. The cuts of fish were fresh.  The wait staff were attentive. I will definitely go back again. Great value at $55!

Awesome Omakase spot, i’ve been here 3 times already and it doesn’t get old. Super efficient (45 minutes for 13 courses) & quality sushi. Only $55 and a no tip restaurant but still super attentive service. Would recommend getting a reservation as they are usually full for walk ins.

Great food. Great vibe. Great service. We had a great time and definitely will be coming back.
Excellent food and service! I had the Royal Japchae and it so savory and delicious! I also enjoyed the Iced Matcha with Oatmilk. The food is made with love. Give it a try 😋

Most delicious pitas, best bangs for the bucks in town. Southern chicken and the kebabs are my favorites. And they have tahini ice cream!

Walking into this spot you're greeted with a cozy and "at home" feel. Growing up eating my mom's cooking I have yet to find a restaurant that can compare to that level of authenticity and love that Sami & Susu provided tonight. Their sommelier is knowledgeable beyond words and brought the experience to another level. Truly a great meal from beginning to end, thank you Jordan and Amir.

Cozy little walk in with two tables and a bar, wings slap got 16 wings half boneless half w/ bone and 2 soda for $20, boneless wings are also more like tenders in the crunch and chicken meat texture which i was pleasantly surprised about. Auntie Tina was awesome and the chef was also very kind and hospitable. You can’t beat wings at these prices and they taste great. They also have a small outdoor seating set up. I got the Cajun rub and hot buffalo. Would recommend both. This place is great. I will back.

Love this place! 100% would always go again

Almost got scammed by the staff, Ordered 2 large Ice latte, he asked the same question for 3times for tri-confirmation, then he provided us one large and one small latte, when asked about it, he literally showed damn care  about his mistake. And that latte taste is below average. 👎

Amazing haven for the cats & the greater community! So glad to see these cats so well cared for and loved - Leila was superb & phenomenal along with the rest of the team! Sad this place can’t stay open but the spirit of Koneko lives on!
Leila was such a good person to talk and know more about the cats. Truly someone who cares and it's a shame this place had to close. Lovely staff all around!

I was visiting NYC with my cousin for her birthday, she found Koneko and was very excited to go. It was a great way to start our day, a nice calm, quiet place with the most adorable cats. It was good to have a slow hour with cats before the rest of our busy day. I had a chai latte and it was yummy!

you have to share a table with others which is not ideal but the food is SO GOOD!! The waiters are all Taishanese so I felt right at home :)

Dishes stand out for freshness and amazing taste. Service is friendly and attentive, setting is clean and simple. I stop by in free time and feel satisfied after every meal. People have different feelings; no food can compare to this for me.
The food tastes amazing. Service is quick and dishes arrive fast after ordering. The whole meal is delicious and satisfying. Highly recommend it to all Chinese food lovers.

We got there on a Friday morning a few minutes before they opened. There was already a line, and we didn’t make it into the restaurant immediately so had to wait a hour and a half, which we spent walking around SoHo. If you’re willing to wait, the food is amazing! Favorites were the tortellini pomodoro, the cucumbers new yorkese, and the affogato!

The tomato martini is truly the most phenomenal martini I’ve ever had. Order a bunch of different things and share amongst your party. Every pasta dish we had melted in our mouths. Such amazing flavor and the pasta was perfectly cooked.

The Cucumbers New Yorkese +  Grapefruit & Fennel Cocktail set the tone for an unbelievable 5th anniversary  dinner. Some of the most unique bites we’ve ever had. Followed up with great pastas were the iconic Pomodoro and the Spicy Jamaican Ragu but the lamb stole the show. No reason to even use the spices. The food, service, wine, energy was so good we forgot to take a picture!

I’ve been here twice now. The first time, I got in line at 10:45am and was able to be seated at their bar when they opened at 11:30am. They have limited bar seats - maybe 10? You must arrive early and wait in line if you want a chance to get in this way. They may also allow you to request a bar seat for the evening if you do this. No tables will be available, as these are reservation only.

Most recently, I dined with a table reservation last week. Reservations are difficult to snag. I was able to book through Resy after I set up alerts for cancellations. This is only really a reliable method if you have priority status on Resy by being an AMEX platinum card holder, because you will get the alerts first. Despite being 25 minutes late (nyc traffic), they allowed us to sit at our table. We had exceptional service and delicious food. Our server was extremely knowledgeable on our options as vegans. He was able to recommend a cucumber appetizer and two different pastas. The cucumbers were a huge surprise and stole the show. The pastas were also incredible. We were there celebrating our anniversary, and they sent us a beautiful display of fruit on ice in a large bowl and a sorbet dessert.

I would dine at this place during every visit to the city. Highly, highly recommend for anybody and everybody.

Best dive bar in NYC with the best bartender. Andrew is exceptional at what he does. He somehow remembers your order even if you haven’t been in for a while, and makes the best cocktails. The spicy marg is truly out of this world. 10/10, no notes.

My only complain is the portion size is kinda small?? or maybe we just ate too fast lol. we finished it in like 10 mins. Wish they give a little more. The place is old and service is whatever, but purely for the food its totally worth it.

Med rare burger was med edging into med well but not worth complaining over. Still should be getting temp right on a burger. Asparagus ravioli just ok, seemed overwhelmed with truffle. If the desserts are done by a separate dessert chef that chef seems to be in a different class to the head chef as those were excellent. I think this place is heavily driven by excellent cocktails and location and when you are slightly toasted you can ignore some clumsy cooking.
Very nice bar food.

After a long shopping spree in SoHo, the four of us were quite hungry – and stumbled upon Bar Mercer quite by chance. The incredibly warm welcome from Nicholas, the manager, and the stylish, inviting atmosphere immediately won us over, so we spontaneously decided to have dinner there.

To start, we enjoyed a perfectly prepared salmon tartare. For our main courses, we chose filet and sirloin steak. The meat was incredibly tender, superbly seasoned, and grilled to perfection – simply delicious!

The various wines from different wine regions, which we sampled by the glass, were all excellent.

Top marks for the outstanding food, the beautiful ambiance, and the attentive, warm service! We thoroughly enjoyed our evening and would love to return anytime.

We also couldn’t believe that two lobsters were only $38! Their lunch special is only $10 too, which is such a great deal. Great food, generous portions, and very reasonable prices. Definitely a hidden gem and a place I’d happily come back to.

Everything was just SO tasty!! 🤤 My friends come here every week and recommended this place to me, and now I totally understand why. The food is really good quality, portions are huge, and the prices are surprisingly reasonable.

I especially loved the crab fried sticky rice! The texture was perfectly crunchy, and you could really taste how fresh the crab was with every bite. Soooo good! 🦀

I also want to come back and try their lunch specials — they have a pretty wide selection of entrees, and you get an entree + rice + soup for only $10! Such a great deal.

Definitely stop by and give this place a try if you’re in Chinatown.

Definitely one of my favorite Chinese seafood spots in Chinatown! The live lobster was super fresh and delicious, and the walnut shrimp was SO good - big, juicy shrimp with a really nice crunchy texture. Honestly, all the seafood we tried was fresh and tasty.

The prices are also pretty reasonable for the quality. They even have lunch specials with an entree, rice, and soup for only $10, which is a really good deal.

Service was excellent too, and everyone was really nice and welcoming. Definitely recommend this place if you’re into seafood, and I’ll definitely be coming back!

We decided to sit at the bar and the bartender was both friendly and knowledgeable and suggested we try the branzino, which was delicious.  Unfortunately, what had been an overwhelmingly positive experience was spoiled by the manager on duty who was highly disrespectful to the patrons at the bar.  At one point, the manager (female) engaged with a couple at the end of the bar and her behavior was both aggressive and embarrassing and made her staff and everyone in the venue visibly uncomfortable. We decided to pay our tab and head elsewhere.  The food and other staff members were fantastic but we will not be coming back.

The pasta dishes had different meats and cheeses mixed in and were among the best homemade pasta I have had in NYC. Then we shared a branzino which was perfection. We didn't have room for dessert but had the chocolate cake anyway! Wow, what a dessert. Great meal, great service and ambiance. I can't wait to go back!
Excellent trattoria

I look forward to going back again! There are more dishes I need to try!

I've tried this brand of coffee in Paris and Kyoto before, and even then, the last few sips still had a strong coffee flavor, so this was a bit disappointing. I wonder if it was because it was the weekend, but the coffee shop was very crowded, so I couldn't sit down and enjoy my coffee at my own pace.

Great place!  I loved their BBQ wings, popcorn shrimp, and breaded chicken sandwich!  The staff was so friendly and the place itself was very pleasant.  It's such a shame that they're no longer around.

I'll give credit where credit is due, the manager (?) came over and let me know they'd be removing my meal from the bill but that didn't make up for the staff treating us as though we were an inconvenience throughout the entire meal.

DBA: BLUE PEAK VILLA / ZHONG GUO XIAO LONG BAO
review_text:
Food is generally good, and quite spicy. We (party of 5) came here for dinner and had some hits but sadly, some misses too.
The service was atrocious.  It felt uneven at best. There was little coordination among the wait staff, dishes coming out haphazardly, appetizers came after some main dishes, and rice orders missing despite repeated requests. When a fish soup came, we had to go find a waitstaff to ask for bowls; the traditional Chinese bowls finally came but alas, with Western (metal) spoons.
The serving utensils too seemed afterthought: eating forks for soupy dishes, or in some cases, missing serving utensil altogether.
The underground venue, while spacious, was oddly arranged, as if it was hurriedly rearranged from something else. With glass mirror walls in enclosed space, it was not surprising that the noise level was quite unbearable at times.
We were seated at a round table, too large for our group of 5. Some chairs were clearly more suited for art studios (3-legged chairs make unstable dining chairs).

The food was good, but I would stick to takeout orders and skip the dine-in experience.
