review_text: Took my order quickly and got me my bagel pretty fast even though there was a little rush. The bagel itself is okay. On the breadier side. Should be better for the competition in this area. The cream cheese is good.
Best bagels in New York! Came from London for these
They remade my bagel for me no charge. Thank you Pop and crew
Best beagles on NY
V funny

One of the most wonderful stores in New York for a unique sportswear and lounge shopping experience. Everything they have is great and of high quality. I also tried their personal care products, and they were excellent. In addition to the sportswear, I couldn't miss ordering healthy and detox drinks in the drinks section. Everything they have is exceptional.

Beautiful store and incredible staff! I've been to this location a couple of times, every time I get a chance to visit NY. The staff are super friendly and helpful and make the effort to find your sizes and recommend other items. Unfortunately, the store doesn't seem to be fully stocked – a lot of items I was looking at did not have a full size run and many items on display were simply just the last ones available. Considering this and the LA store are the only Sporty & Rich stores, and people definitely make this store a destination, it would help both the customers and the store itself to have more sizes and quantities in stock.

So glad we stopped by, everything was absolutely delicious! I went with the Oreo and my girlfriend got the butterscotch, and both were incredible. We’re already hooked and will definitely be back. Huge shoutout to Jason, too, for being so friendly, attentive, and welcoming!

Excellent service; they have a great team, and it shows in the positive atmosphere. It was our first time visiting the city, and we were very impressed with the quality. Congratulations.

Sin duda si regremos pasaremos la próxima vez con Alejandro y Jacob ya que los visitamos 3 veces en dos semanas !!! 👏👏👏
3% more if you pay by credit card?!!

First time to this location. Really cool design and vibe.
Nice selection of flavors.
Friendly staff

I've never been to a rice pudding shop before, so this was such a treat! I much prefer rice pudding cold, so this was great for me. I went for the pannacotta flavour and it was delish! The smallest (cheapo) size was absolutely plenty in my opinion and the price was decent!
Big crowd and delicious food. A tad pricey.

Delicious food with generous portions, a great happy hour offering, and attentive, kind staff. Not to mention the awesome Star Wars mural downstairs. This place has it all.

After dining here, I was shocked this establishment was not higher reviewed. Looking at the low reviews there is a common thread in that this is not an “authentic” or “contemporary” Vietnamese restaurant. Having never been to Vietnam, I cannot comment on the allegations. However this restaurant deserves a 10!

I could not stop eating! Seriously, the food in this place was a very pleasant surprise.

Our favorite was the charbroiled ribs and the beef broth. So yummy 🤤

We absolutely loved our experience at Saigon Social! The outdoor seating was wonderful, and our waiter, Aaron, provided excellent, attentive service. He even came back after the restaurant closed with a bar recommendation. The food was fantastic. The mussels came in an incredibly flavorful sauce that was perfect for soaking up with the amazing bread. The garlic noodles were one of the best entrees I had— perfectly cooked in another great sauce. If they still have the special where you can get it with crab - do it! We finished with the pandan cheesecake, which was a terrific dessert. Not too rich, but one of the best versions of cheesecake I've had. Fantastic food, warm hospitality, and a lovely atmosphere (especially sitting outside on a weekend). We can’t wait to return!
If you are vegan come here NOW!!!!

Delicious ice cream

Areas for improvement:

- Portion rather small
- Service could have been friendlier
- Unfortunately, plastic spoons were used

A nice little ice cream shop serving delicious ice cream, especially the “MADORLA DI-TORITTO” flavor - almond flavored. The ice cream is creamy and doesn't turn watery as it melts. They also serve crêpes. It's a small place with only a few chairs for seating, but definitely worth a visit.

This is a truly excellent rooftop bar! Plenty of space inside and spectacular views outside of lower Manhattan. We were here during a rainy night and the west side has outdoor heaters (not covered otherwise).The happy hour is good considering NYC ($13 wine, $16 cocktails) and just overall chill vibes. Not too loud and DJs slapped on a Sunday

My only complaint in which will not be docked for is they only had 1 white and 1 red wine offered tonight but cocktails were tasty.

Well, we didn’t get to try food here, the drinks are really good and the view was amazing. It wasn’t too crowded so you could still enjoy your time there, but there were enough people that it was lively and a fun atmosphere

Definitely recommend this rooftop bar for amazing views of Lower Manhattan! We had a great time with our company. Always polite and friendly staff will not leave you unattended, the most delicious and refreshing summer cocktails will give you even more mood, as well as unbeatable snacks and desserts from the chef - all this you can find in the “Unlisted” bar !👍👍👍
Decent views, but just a sad city rooftop bar. So many better places to go.
Went here for a mixer, the views were great and the staff was lovely
The food is so delicious! The tacos are too good
Great place I love it here
Stellar mushroom bowl, pico, and quac. Highly recommend.

Stopped by the market to grab some groceries and stopped at the Catalyst Market bar. I knew about the Catalyst record shop which is diagonally located. Had an artisanl hot dog from the famed butchery Ends Meat and an americano cocktail. This was the perfect pause to an otherwise very hectic day. Where can you get a cocktail for under $15 in NYC? This isnt a dive bar pour of a G&T in a plastic cup with a nasty lemon. Great vibe and a true local spot run by local residents. Highly recommend. Thanks Gary!

Great casual neighborhood bar in the heart of Essex Market. I stopped on my way to a movie and it was a great warm up for a snack, and a quick spritz before the movie. The price point is what stood out given how expensive everything generally is. Great location, great vibe and price. Highly recommend.
Best mochi I’ve had! Staff were super friendly and they have boba with horchata too. Honestly a must try in the area
Tried the passion fruit cheesecake mochi and the matcha bec that is what was recommended to me. So good! Would def have again! The passionfruit was surprisingly good
Great manager, delicious yuzu lemonade
Hands down the best mochi ice cream in the city.  The salt caramel is amazing.

Least enthusiastic bartender in Manhattan.  4 people in bar ....more than 15 minutes to get a drink.  Food took 40 minutes and came out cold.  A few people quietly chatting and music was 160-180 bpm edm and dance pop....I'm a dj, I like it but it was all wrong for the night.
good soup :)
Super chill spot with amazing cocktails and friendly vibes
A superb Italian restaurant, delicious with authentic Italian flavors, I highly recommend it.

I visited Tre simply because its location was right next door to the hotel I was staying at. It’s a very small lowkey type of restaurant. I ordered the calamari. This calamari was hands down the BEST calamari I’ve ever eaten! Tre also introduced to a new delicious cocktail. I’d 100% visit Tre again on my next NYC adventure. I give them an A+.

5/5!!!! I absolutely loved this place, and I will definitely be back!

First things first—make a reservation! They get BOOKED and BUSY! My brother and I took a chance and walked in, but luckily we were able to grab seats at the bar, which honestly wasn't bad at all.

It's a small, cozy spot with a really comfortable vibe. The service was great, the atmosphere was inviting, and the food did not disappoint.

My total came to about $80 for my share, which included appetizers, an entrée, a shared dessert, taxes, gratuity, and unlimited wine for two hours. That is an absolute steal for everything you get!

And can we talk about the bruschetta?! It was AMAZING—easily one of my favorite things we ordered. I can't wait to come back and try more from the menu! Let’s keep this place on the hush hush though because I do not want EVERYBODY coming then definitely there will be no space lol😂😩
LOVED these tacos!
They are now serving dollar pizza for triple the price. Used to go here all the time but they changed the recipe and it’s now soggy small and flavorless. Change the recipe back please!

Had a dozen pizza pies delivered to an event. The cheese pizza was good - delivered and hot. The pepperoni pie was a bit sparse on the pepperoni, and less cheese. Paper plates and napkins were included.
Bestest experience for my 5 year old, so many exciting things to do! Loved that each station was allergen friendly and had so many delicious vegan ice cream options!
Very fun and adventurous my kid had soooo much fun and wishes to live there definitely recommend
My daughter had so much fun we had a hard time leaving lol

i had their chocolate chip cookies and they were very good. i always wanted to come because i saw it in the movie loser. yes i love my romantic comedies from the year 2000 :) but anyway very good place.

i also got their "rainbow" cookies. they were green and beige with the almond paste. so good! my parents loved them too. i also got the loaf of ciabatta bread. wow! i was blown away with how fresh it was. i brought it home. loved that there was so much flour on it too :). its my weakness. its so soft in the middle and crunchy on the outside. my parents went crazy over it. the only downside is that they don't slice it for you but its ok i still wanna buy it again!
Very good focaccia and pignoli cookies. Staff is always great
A very cute bakery I've been wanting to try. I had the apple pie and tea 🍎

We wanted to go inside the place, but before doing so, we took a few photos of my girlfriend on the outdoor couch while enjoying our Sunday off. An employee came outside and told us that we were only allowed to take photos if we purchased something from the place, and the way he approached us was very unfriendly. We immediately left because of the way we were treated, especially when we were simply appreciating the beautiful space they have. It’s unfortunate that such a lovely place can be overshadowed by poor customer service and the way people are treated.

Came from a recommendation for my friend. I asked Charles "what's the best pastry you have?" He recommended a cookie that was so good, I don't even know what it was exactly! I will be back for something else!
Maddie was so nice and helpful! I’m a big soda girl and this was exactly what I wanted!!! She was also so sweet. Def recommend!!!

I was helped by Maddie and she was SO AMAZING. So easy to talk to and was super helpful helping us decide what we wanted. The menu could be more diverse but I always think that the environment of the store is the most important thing.
Girl at the counter today was so beautiful and sweet I forgot to taste my drink 10/10

I had never been here before and was quite overwhelmed with all the options i had to choose from. Maddie was so kind at helping me choose my own personalized drink. Very organized and clean. I WILL be coming back. Thank you Maddie !

Never knew what a dirty soda was till now, I’m glad I stopped by! I got the classic dirty dirty it was very refreshing and light !
Staff was very nice and helped me when I was clearly struggling lol will be back !
Very tasty and good quality chocolate !! Loved the Cookie with big chocolate chunks 😛

Awesome hot chocolate but extremely unfriendly woman behind the bar. Yes, the African American one. Tried to make conversation with her but just got a blank stare like she was really annoyed by having to help me. She must be the owner if she’s still there. Won’t come back here again. Also No acknowledgement when entering or leaving the store by her or the other 3 people working there.
Terrible tasting chocolates. Chocolates are so hard to get wrong but here we are. Sad that I can’t enjoy this box the way I thought I would.
Good food, efficient service. It's a solid lunch place.
ordered it from uber eats, they never delivered, never picked up the phone. unbelievable. would not recommend for sure.
They did not give me utensils in my Togo order. How am I supposed to eat this?  I cannot get it from anywhere near me.
Service is amazing and food was perfect.

Enjoyed a really great pre-movie dinner here with a friend. Started with the beef tartare, which was great, then had the Caesar salad with grilled chicken, again fantastic, and ended with a delicious tangerine sorbet. It is pricey, but the food and atmosphere is fantastic. Highly recommend.
Had a great lunch visit today. A special shoutout to Ethan, our server, who was incredibly kind, accommodating, and helpful throughout our visit!
ETHAN WAS THE BEST!! Love him for his service and friendliness and charm :)
Amazing tartine sandwiches and juices.  The soups are also very good. Good prices and the staff is very attentive and great.  Everything a European cafe should be.  A 15/10 experience.
Best Pommes Frites in NYC… service could be better the location and outdoor sitting is good.

Can’t even ask for my onions to be grilled/not raw.

Also the last time I went they mistook my order, and took forever to arrive.

DIG is one of the best places I’ve been for a fresh, satisfying meal and excellent service. The team is fast, friendly, and welcoming, and the generous portions offer outstanding value—especially in New York City.

At $14 for a bowl with four choices, or $17 for the salmon option, the pricing is hard to beat. Many restaurants charge $20–$25 for a single entrée, sometimes with additional charges for rice or sauces.

What truly stands out is the team’s commitment to their customers. They consistently go above and beyond to make sure you leave happy. Great food, fair prices, and exceptional service—I highly recommend it!

Really cheap on the meat serving. They count like every tiny piece. $16 for a bowl of 90% carbs and fat and 10% meat is a rip off. Would not recommend. They are trying to scam people into paying for double meat by making the included serving ridiculously small.
Heaven and Tara were amazing it was almost time to close and they were so outgoing and nice
The girl with the glasses is goated, love this place
Awesome service and food
Wonderful!
Very good!
Incredible food. Best sushi in the city. Must try!!
very nice staff

One of the better dining halls at NYU. Most of the servers are pretty friendly and they have a nice variety of fresh food and different cuisines. Their knock-off CAVA bowls are pretty tasty. Chicken tenders are pretty fire. Coca-cola freestyle machine is super convenient. Would recommend.

Luis is the only serious burger maker. if you dont get him choose something else that day. Samba is also a very cool dude. Makes school not seem so hellish. The food is just okay most of the time, but is overpriced if you dont have a meal swipe. Chicken tenders is always consistent. A lot of times I use the salad bar to spruce up my meal.
Super overpriced. I will not eat here if I don't have to use meal plan.
Everything it is amazing!!!

Excellent food. A fantastic atmosphere, with the perfect balance of a quiet place for dinner and a lively vibe with music. The staff's friendliness is outstanding, far surpassing most others. You can feel the friendly and helpful Italian spirit. 10 out of 10.
Food was good, but portions were quite small and WAY overpriced. Service was just okay. I would avoid

This restaurant was such a great experience. We met the owner at the door! We got a lovely table in the back garden. The chef made an excellent off menu chicken piccata for one of our group. We had eggplant parmesan, vegetarian lasagna special, and enjoyed everything.

Got a dankwrap as part of New York magazine subscription’s monthly perks. The staff were very accommodating, because I was slightly embarrassed of availing my perk. The wrap was standard affair. Had it in Washington square park.

The staff went above and beyond my expectations. I will be back 🌯✨

It was DANK!
Great food and service
Cozy seating and wonderful service! We had a really lovely time and thoroughly enjoyed our experience. Highly recommend!

We came for the mapo tofu, and it was exquisite! The Peking duck was also exceptional—you could really taste the quality. Our server was the sweetest and made the experience even more special. We’d happily come back!
Awesome place beautiful ambience. I will come here every week for the rest of my life

Had the worst restaurant experience ever in this place. Lousy service (we waited an hour for the food to arrive), food is mediocre at best, the space is super tight and uncomfortable and the price on some of the items we ordered were wrong! And here's the worst part: THEY CHARGED US 22% TIP INSTEAD OF THE 20% INDUSTRY STANDARD FOR A BIG GROUP! AND ON TOP OF THAT - THEY SLIPPED A $24 "HANDLING/CONVENIENCE FEE"! What kind of restaurant tries to slip a convenience fee on customers?! That is definitely ILLEGAL! We disputed all these abhorrent charges through the credit card company because this restaurant won't pick up the phone nor respond to any of our messages! DO YOURSELF A FAVOR - AVOID THIS RESTAURANT AT ALL COST!

The service, music, ambiance, and food here are absolutely amazing! From the moment we walked in, the staff was incredibly friendly and attentive, making us feel welcome right away.
Their cocktail game is top-tier, the drinks are perfectly balanced with a creative twist. We started with a dirty martini, a mezcal penicillin, and a glass of wine, all of which were excellent. For appetizers, we ordered the crispy tuna fries and the hamachi. Both were incredibly fresh, but what really stands out is how unique the sauces are. Everything is prepared to absolute perfection.
For our main course, we split the duck adobo and the fried rice, and it did not disappoint. During dinner, Chef Josh actually came over to our table to talk to us. He shared the inspiration behind the menu, explaining his incredible fusion of French and Filipino culinary styles, and mentioned that his mentor worked with Jean-Georges for a long time. You can truly taste that world-class pedigree in every single bite.
I highly recommend coming to this restaurant for an unforgettable meal. Plus, if you are looking to keep the night going, they transition into a club after 10 PM. We will definitely be back!
Great place I would definitely recommend coming here if your out in town

I went here for my birthday a few months ago and absolutely loved every minute of dinner; from the waitstaff’s service to the chef coming out to explain the dishes to the food itself! Such a perfectly intentional menu and the ideal spot for a special occasion. This place has been on my mind lately and I will definitely be back soon!!!
I got an iced vanilla latte with extra ice and sugar free vanilla with almond milk and a cookie butter cookie. The cookie is tasty. However the latte is way too sweet and milky.
Nutella latte didn’t taste like anything it was a regular latte with Nutella slathered on sides of the cup??? Why sell something if you are not going to make it well??? And it was $10
Amazing! Salted caramel cold foam cold brew is super good.
It’s simply amazing, a cozy cafe either great coffee and an extremely sweet barista, made my day!
From the flavor options to the mellow vibes all 💯 enjoyable.
Could be better with little more food on plate.
Food was fantastic; super old school vibes. If you’re looking for a good Italian meal in a cozy restaurant this is a great spot
Old school classic Italian food. Everything delicious and service is always amazing

Unfortunately on our second visit my wife contracted extreme food poisoning from the special that night. We are 100% certain it was her dish as I only sampled on small bite of her order and this was out first food we had in eight hours up to this meal. Knowing food safety is pivotal to a fine restaurant like Monte's, we were not looking for any restitution or any comensation. But s half hearted "We're sorry", just didn't sit well with us. Bloody diarrhea for four days and a trip to Lennox Hill Hospital was not on our plans for a trip to NYC. We really love Monte's, but after this experience I believe we'll not be going back.
Wow - amazing, legit Italian in a 100-year old restaurant. Ask for Danny and get Chef Pietro’s tiramisu!  Incredible.
Very good vegetarian tamales. The salsa verde zucchini was excellent. Good horchata too. FYI no bathroom.
Great vegan Tamales!
Yum
The pastries are good, but the ice cream is the best. The Ube ice cream sandwich is insane, and I don't even like Ube that much. You also can't go wrong with the gelato, especially the pandan one.

Very overpriced for what you get. I ordered the ice cream sandwich, and it was practically melted inside the bag when I received it. It was a mess and nearly impossible to eat properly. Definitely not worth the price.
I ordered a pint of the pandan kaya jam gelato. It wasn’t packed in all the way and there was an ice cube at the bottom 🫩

Got their ube pandan banana pudding and it was so yummy 😋 Haven’t tried anything like these 3 ingredients together and they complemented really well. The place is either yet to be fully established or still in the initial setup phase. Its in a warehouse type place with some chairs and tables. Will surely visit to try their rest items.

Fun, design-forward bakehouse on Rivington. The space is all steel and red neon, and the pastry case is full of creative stuff like the crème brûlée donut and a spicy croissant. The ube pastry was the standout for me. Knocking one star because the crème brûlée and the doughnuts leaned a little too sweet for my taste. Still very much worth a stop if you are in the neighborhood.

So glad to have found this restaurant. The food comes in great portion. Definitely worth the prices that you’re paying. Foods were alittle on the spicy side and have a slight spice kicks in them, which was great for me. I went during lunch hour and it was about 10ish minutes wait to be seated, which was not a problem for me. The servers were nice and helpful. I will definitely be going back again to try more foods on the menu.

I was yearning for a good Thai place and I found it!! The ingredients are fresh and the flavours are strong, exactly what you need from a real Thai restaurant. We had the cabbage rolls, the egg sandwich the banana chicken and the salad rolls. Everything was great. Definitely recommend!
yummy and delesyou

Beautiful decor inside and out, and the breakfast sandwich is not only one of the best things I've ever had in Nyc but possibly one of the tastiest and most interesting things I have ever eaten. I wanted to go back the next day! Service was also lovely (great tattoos too!)

The place is definitely busy, but the staff does a great job of keeping things moving, so the wait is never too long! The food is amazing, and the staff is just as wonderful. Our server Brian was incredible. Definitely worth the visit!

My favorite affordable happy hour in the city. I’ve been going for almost 4 years. They know me and it’s all love when I come through. One thing is, if you can afford normal sushi, please allow the kids to have this happy hour spot. The young artist ls of the LES aren’t able to eat here anymore because these people form the WV and UES, midtown and wherever are taking up the space. I used to come here and chill with my friends laugh and eat affordable food, now randoms are taking over, same with FMN.
Delicious food and excellent service
Super yummy. Great happy hour.

Breakfast burrito came with chopped green peppers, red peppers and basil rather than mango salad, Which is great because I am allergic to green peppers and would of never ordered anything containing green peppers. Seemingly they ran out of mango salad and decided to substitute without letting me know. Pretty unsafe practices.

Asked politely for a little more matcha because my latte was pale and was told no because this is the standard amount they use. Unsurprisingly only tasted like milk. Also got a pink smoothie that wasn’t blended well, it was full of chunks and the lavender in it overpowered any other flavor. Service was apathetic and cold.

Save your money

Took a fat minute for the waiter to acknowledge my existence in there. Paid an insulting amount for the green smoothie and the first disgusting sip felt like a childhood anorexia relapse. Will totally be back💚
attitude from workers were horrible and disrespectful.
I love it here always especially when I can pick up ACQ bakery living bread but also deli sides and also little gifts it’s expensive but it’s quality

I stopped by Gold Coffee in Manhattan while waiting for my Uber Shuttle to JFK. It's right in front of the shuttle stop, so the location is perfect, and it was nice to grab a cold drink on a hot day.
The staff were extremely friendly. I asked for something decaf, cold, and dairy-free, and they didn't mind me being picky. I really enjoyed the ordering experience, and the chai I got was really good too.
If you're waiting for the shuttle here, I'd definitely recommend stopping in.

Espresso was well pulled, and the cold brew was strong without being harsh. But there are maybe four stools, and all were occupied when I came in. Ended up taking mine to go, which was fine; just don't plan on sitting down. Around $7.
BEST coffee i’ved had in the U.S. I discovered this place a couple of weeks ago and I have come here everyday since. The host is very welcoming. I would definitely recommend!!

Amazing coffee, Elton is great host. Proper Albanian coffee and hospitality. Everyone needs to try this place at least once! If you come to New York, here’s the place to have coffee and so many other things.

This spot Permanently closed shut down!!
Dubai chocolate taste terrible I got food poisoning! employees stand around service too slow!   i recommend visiting  LAZA DESSERT IN BK it’s scrumptious!!
Is this spot actually closed?! I hope not, loved their chocolate covered strawberries😭
Brother Ali in front is best guy I recommend
Not the same anymore.
Unfortunately, they changed their packaging and the cups are small now, and the prices are the same. It sucks cause this was my go to for late night soft serve, but I guess no more.

I used to order almost weekly but absolutely never again. They moved locations, changed ownership, raised prices, and reduced quality of food and service (even further).

I ordered delivery with a 20+% tip. This was advertised as 25mins, given I am less than 10 blocks away.

At the THREE hour mark (ordered at 1:45pm, got a notification at 4:45pm), they marked it as delivered on their end. Thus they wasted hours of my time, LIED about delivering my order when I received nothing nor any contact from them, and now I have to find a way refund my order.

Absolutely ridiculous as a business. Much better to go to Prankahon at this point since they moved close by and raised prices.

EDIT: I couldn’t get my 20% tip refunded. Forever lost a loyal customer.
Great spot! Highly recommend
So tasteful and so little oil I can see the white of the plate beneath the noodles. Banana peppers for the spice, with bell peppers for the crunch and flavor is so apt
miss this place
Friendly staff, very chill vibes

If you're ok compromising a little on comfort and spotty service for excellent food, you're going to love 12 Chairs. Everything was fresh and delicious.  Can't recommend any one specific dish, because it was all fantastic.  But, there's a reason why it's called 12 Chairs.  It's tight, fairly uncomfortable, and much better for a casual, social meal than a business one. Servers work hard, but there's just not enough of them. Then, again, there probably isn’t enough room to add more of them. The restaurant is pleasing on the eye, just typical Village tight spaces. Go for the food experience, and you won't be disappointed.  And, after all, that's what matters most.

12 Chairs is an absolutely charming Israeli spot in SoHo and a wonderful find. The food is fresh and delicious, the ambiance is delightful, and there's always a fun, lively vibe. The staff is super friendly and makes you feel right at home.

Insider tip: there are four "secret" stools at the bar in the back, and that's hands down my favorite place to sit. It's a classic hip, small NYC café with tables close together and an eclectic crowd, which is a big part of its charm. Highly recommend!

12 Chairs is a longtime favorite of ours--perfect for breakfast, lunch dinner. Last night we took out of town friends there for dinner--their first time. Everyone was thrilled with the quality of the food, excellent service, sense of fun in the air. It's definitely not a place for quiet conversation--but perfect for a delicious meal and buzzy vibe.
Felipe, Rafa, panda and frank the entire staff have been amazing! One of my Favorite spots 🤞🏽
Great spot to bring a new girl or friend great food and service as well and  a great atmosphere

So Resy/Google let me make a reservation for Tuesday at 6:30pm and yet when I arrived they’re closed? Their website AND instagram says that they open at 5pm on Tuesdays but Google says their closed. This is very annoying and inconvenient to my evening plans
It is not a Romanian restaurant.

Took my dad out for dinner here for his birthday…we are Romanian and this restaurant is “Romanian-ish” which we appreciated!! Very tasty food that did not disappoint. Loved the vibe and the fact that it’s tapas style: shareable little plates. Our favorite was the stuffed pepper: both sweet and smoky and delicious. The fasole batuta which is a bean dip tasted very authentic. My dad looooved the burrata. The mici (little Romanian sausages) did not taste very much like the mici we are used to but they were fine, even  better paired with the pickled spicy grapes. Mamaliga was delicious. Service was great. They knew we were celebrating a birthday and brought over a little plate with gummy bears and a lit candle, super thoughtful gesture and very appreciated. Loved the whole dining experience here and would absolutely return and recommend.
Really well executed, unique brunch items, lovely one man show.

It’s difficult to put into a short review how wonderful this restaurant is and how delicious their food is. You perfectly encapsulate every yummy flavor that is Romanian food. It’s the most intimate cozy lovely little gem. I grew up on my mom and bunică‘s Romanian home-cooked meals, and all the dishes at Oti taste just like those sentimental dishes from my childhood, but with a unique and thoughtful twist.
Please go eat there. I’m always proud to be Romanian, and this little restaurant quietly nestled in the Lower East Side makes me even more proud and reminds me of home.
We had a great time here and an especially great experience with our server George was very attentive.
No personality. It feels off.  I miss the old Carole Place had lots of charm and identity. Now it’s just blah.  It’s doesn’t know what it is.
Love Yesterdays! George is the best!!

I wasn’t a huge fan of my experience here. From the moment I walked in, the bouncer made me uncomfortable. He bent my ID and had to double-check it, even though I’m clearly over the legal age.

Once we were seated, we waited about 45 minutes for our entrées. The first thing that came out was the cinnamon rolls, and honestly, they were the best thing I had the entire time. Everything else was disappointing and severely underseasoned.

The French onion slider sauce tasted like absolutely nothing—water had more flavor. The chicken tenders were crispy and decent, but they definitely needed salt. The mozzarella sticks didn’t even feel like real mozzarella sticks; the cheese seemed frozen and there wasn’t even a cheese pull. The fries came out cold, and somehow all of the salt was sitting at the bottom of the plate instead of actually being on the fries. The burrito was also extremely bland and lacked seasoning.

The customer service didn’t make the experience any better. Our waiter took our order and basically disappeared. He never came back to check on us. Another employee was checking on other tables, but we had to repeatedly try to make eye contact before she finally came over to help us. At that point, it felt like the main concern was making sure we paid rather than making sure we were enjoying our meal.

I originally came here because I saw it on TikTok, but unfortunately, it did not live up to the hype at all. Between the food, the long wait, and the customer service, I don’t see myself coming back anytime soon. They definitely need to improve both the seasoning and the overall customer experience.

And honestly, based on the name, maybe I should’ve known—the food tasted like yesterday’s meal. Nothing memorable and definitely nothing I’d recommend.

this is my favorite matcha place in the city. the matcha is not sweet and super strong which i love. their speciality flavors are always so good like the pumpkin one right now, and every time i go i have to get the matcha brownie, it’s the best thing ever.

i’ve liked matchaful for years, especially their matcha soft serve, so this is coming from someone who genuinely wanted to keep liking the brand. i went to the soho location and got the 16 oz mango cold foam matcha for $11.43 after tax (it’s one sized so the price being that is even more questioning hmm). the staff were excellent - i took a good 3–6 minutes deciding, asked questions, changed my mind a few times, and they stayed patient, gave recommendations, and never made me feel rushed. the space is also nice, especially the seating along the windows if you want to sit for a bit.

the drink itself tasted good, but this is where i have a problem with the price. the mango was strong, creamy, and easily the dominant flavor. the matcha was so subtle that my immediate comparison was honestly mango lassi with matcha somewhere in the background. if this were an $8-ish fruit drink, i probably wouldn’t think much of it. at $11.43 from a business built around matcha, i expected the tea itself to be one of the most noticeable parts of the drink.

i actually looked into the recipe afterward because i didn’t want to complain about the price just because “$11 sounds expensive.” matchaful lists 4g of hikari matcha, mango purée, housemade oat milk, agave, and mango-coconut cold foam. their hikari is legitimately well-sourced japanese matcha, so i’m not accusing them of using cheap powder. there are real ingredients and extra prep here.

but researching it also made me less convinced by the value, not more. other serious matcha shops are able to make the tea itself much more central at lower prices. kettl, one of the more established japanese tea specialists in nyc, also uses 4g in its own latte recipe and literally describes its approach as making the matcha the star. current listings put its iced ceremonial matcha latte around $7.50. 12 matcha is another very matcha-focused shop using first-harvest matcha, and recent customer reports put a latte around the same $7–8 range.

obviously those are not identical drinks. matchaful is adding mango and a separate cold foam, so an upcharge makes sense. i’m not expecting a specialty fruit drink to cost exactly the same as a plain latte. i just don’t think mango, oat milk and cold foam automatically bridge the gap to an almost $12 experience when the most expensive and supposedly distinctive ingredient was one of the least noticeable things i tasted.

and to be fair, matchaful isn’t uniquely doing this. there are other nyc specialty matcha shops charging around $10–11 before tax for elaborate fruit matchas with cold foam. so this is partly where the market is going. but “other places charge this much too” explains the price —> it doesn’t automatically prove the value.

that’s really where i land on matchaful. i’m not upset that premium matcha costs money. i’ll happily pay more when i can actually taste why i’m paying more. what bothered me here is that the premium sounded much clearer on the ingredient list than it tasted in the cup.

the service was genuinely great, the atmosphere was nice, and i enjoyed drinking it. i’m not calling it a bad drink. i just think there’s a meaningful difference between a drink being good and a drink being worth $11.43.

overall: great service, nice atmosphere, thoughtful ingredients, enjoyable flavor, but weak matcha presence and poor value at this price. i’d still come back for the soft serve or try something more matcha-forward, but i would not order this particular drink again for or any other drink adding up to $11.43 😿.

After scouring the New York dining scene to pick the right restaurant for a weekend trip in NYC, Corima caught my eye. Great location, stylish dining room, and an original menu in a city with a myriad of mediocre, overpriced Mexican.

At the suggestion of our server, we bought into the tasting menu with drink pairing (mostly because he said it was the only part of the menu that included a taco). As a product of the US-Mexico border, the concept of high-end north Mexican food seemed intriguing, but ultimately fell flat. Several poorly-paced courses and $600 later, we left hungry and disappointed. This felt like everything wrong with NYC’s overhyped dining scene, and the fact that a tortilla was the best and most original thing on the menu was insulting. I do not understand the hype, and the accolades continue to confuse me.

**Taco pictured for reference.

Got the tasting menu with the alcohol tasting pairing menu too.

The meal was amazing. Many small courses and small shots of tequilas to pair with it.

So many interesting exotic and unusual but delicious flavors.

The food at Corima is honestly wonderful: creative, surprising and, most importantly, really delicious. There were several dishes I absolutely loved, which is why I was a little sad that the overall experience didn’t quite feel like five stars to me. The food itself is the clear highlight, and I would genuinely love to return, especially to try the à la carte menu.

The tasting menu included some excellent and memorable dishes. However, I didn’t realise when booking through Resy that the tasting menu was the only option attached to our reservation. We weren’t shown a food menu or asked whether we preferred the tasting menu or à la carte. Later, I saw the couple next to us enjoying beautiful full-sized dishes and realised that à la carte was also available. Maybe I missed something while booking, but I really wish I had known, as their dinner looked like my dream meal. Personally, I would much rather have three amazing dishes and more than one bite of each than thirteen tiny courses.

Unfortunately, the service and communication sometimes felt less polished than I had expected. When we arrived, there was nobody at the entrance, so we — along with another couple — walked into the restaurant before eventually coming back to find someone.

I had also mentioned some food intolerances in my reservation and was told that the restaurant had tried several times to contact me by phone and email. I may have missed calls while travelling, but I never received an email. In the end, I explained that they were intolerances rather than allergies and that I could be flexible, so it wasn’t really an issue, it was just the communication side that felt a little odd.

There were also a few moments during the meal when clearer communication would have helped. We ordered the tortilla with caviar after seeing it at the table next to us. It arrived without caviar and without explanation. We asked again and ordered another one with caviar, but that one also arrived without it. Only when we asked a second time were we told that they had run out. Of course, restaurants run out of things, and that is absolutely no problem; I would simply have appreciated being told before the dish arrived twice.

Something similar happened when we asked to add one of the à la carte dishes we had seen at the neighbouring table. We made clear that we didn’t want to change the tasting menu, but simply wanted to add and pay for another dish. We were told that someone would check, but nobody came back to us. Once dessert arrived, we understood that it wasn’t happening.

None of these things individually is a major issue, and everyone on the team was genuinely lovely and kind. I think I simply expected the experience to feel a little more effortless and attentive at a Michelin-starred restaurant. The food absolutely deserves the praise, and I would happily come back to Corima, particularly to try the à la carte menu. I just wish the service and communication had been a little more refined and had made us feel slightly more looked after, because with food this good, that would have made the evening exceptional.

We arrived at Corima with a reservation, but no table was available, so we were seated at the bar. A few minutes later, the staff told us a table would open in about 15 minutes. We were eventually seated near the bar, rather than in the main dining room.

We ordered two beers while at the bar, but they never reached us after we moved to a table just a few feet from the bartender. We ordered wine instead. From that point on, the service was excellent: attentive and cordial.

The room was buzzing, but so noisy that conversation was difficult. The food, unfortunately, did not justify the excitement or the prices.

The much-touted sourdough flour tortilla with recado negro butter was more like a gooey crepe, accompanied by butter I found tasteless. The cucumber, quelites, piparra, melon, and salsa macha dish was fresh and beautifully presented, though I couldn’t detect the melon. It was good, but the description was more compelling than the dish.

The wagyu beef and heart were well prepared and arranged in a handful of carefully cut pieces. There was very little to eat for the price. The turbot with epazote pil-pil and spring onions was the most interesting dish: it arrived with a hard skin enclosing flavorful, steaming fish. I would have liked more epazote, which seemed lost on the plate.

Overall, Corima was a disappointment. Whatever the restaurant calls its cuisine, the meal bore little resemblance to the Mexican food I know and love. I can think of many restaurants where I would eat better, enjoy the atmosphere more, and spend less. I would not return simply because a place is trending; the food has to be the main event.

We had come for the fusion, that New York meeting of Hispanic and Chinese food, which is hardly a wild idea in this city. You would think someone in the building could talk about it. The waitress could not. Questions got hesitant, flummoxed half-answers, with no opinion and no sense of what was worth ordering. She set the plates down and left. Water was not refilled. A premade iced tea and a straw took about ten minutes. We were in the back booth by the bathroom, along one narrow walkway, so there was nowhere for her to pretend she was not passing us. She did, ten or twelve times, without a word, clearly clocking whether we were done. In a room that small, a stare is not subtle. The attention arrived for the exit and never for the meal. It felt scrutinized, and a little discriminatory.

The portions were generous for the price, and that is the only credit I will give. The food was greasy, overcooked, and mushy, oversalted and still underseasoned, with a gamey edge that belonged to neither tradition. The broccoli beside the sesame chicken was the best thing on the table, which is a miserable thing to have to admit. Everything else tasted like a five-minute search for the dish it was supposed to be. A bastardization. The drinks were the same failure in a glass: too tart and sour, or so sweet the fruit had disappeared.

I can speak for the Chinese side. The people with me can speak for the Hispanic side. None of us took this as gospel, and none of us were impressed. This city already has rooms that love both cuisines, and rooms that fuse them without embarrassing either one. This was the neighborhood worn as a costume. An overrated cash grab, with none of the love and none of the craft. I would not go back.

I completely understand how busy brunch can get, especially on weekends and holidays, but I wish there were some flexibility. I tried making a reservation for Mother’s Day because I wanted to bring my mom, but unfortunately, that wasn’t an option.

I also wanted to mention the menu changes following the renovations. The restaurant itself looks beautiful, and I appreciate the updates, but I genuinely miss the original steak frites. It used to be one of my favorite dishes on the menu! While I appreciate the addition of the smothered steak, the changes to the steak frites have been disappointing, and I’ve found myself coming in for dinner much less frequently because of it.

Despite these few critiques, I really do love Dudley’s. It’s a place I consistently return to, recommend to others, and genuinely enjoy supporting. I was just here yesterday and I’m already coming back today!

I hope this feedback is received in the spirit it’s intended. I’m sharing it because I’ve been a loyal customer for years and would love to see a few of the things that originally made this place so special return. Dudley’s is still one of my favorites, and I look forward to many more visits!

I am genuinely disturbed by how I was treated by the owner of Beyond the Pale, Domhnall Byrnes, last night.

I came to the bar for a friend’s birthday party, for which she had rented out the space. Domhnall was working the door and, while speaking to me, told me to look at him. I have strabismus, an eye condition that affects the alignment of my eyes, so looking directly at someone in the way he was demanding is not always something I can control. I calmly explained this to him.

Instead of showing even a basic level of understanding, Donald accused me of having an “attitude” and told me I could not come inside. I had not been disrespectful or confrontational with him. I was simply trying to explain a physical condition that is completely outside of my control.

What made the experience even more upsetting was that I was there to celebrate a friend’s birthday at an event she had specifically rented the bar for, and I ultimately had to apologize to Donald (despite having done nothing wrong) just so that I would be allowed inside.

No customer should be humiliated or denied entry because a physical condition is misinterpreted. As a woman, and particularly as someone with a condition that affects the way I make eye contact, being spoken to and treated this way by the owner of an establishment was incredibly upsetting. I left the interaction feeling singled out, embarrassed, and unwelcome over something I cannot control.

I hope Domhnall takes some time to reflect on how he treats customers, particularly people with disabilities or physical differences that may affect the way they communicate or interact. No one should have to disclose a medical condition at the door of a bar and then apologize for it in order to be treated with basic dignity.

Based on my experience, I cannot recommend supporting an establishment whose owner treats a customer this way, particularly after being explicitly told that the behavior he was criticizing was the result of a physical condition.

There are plenty of other bars within a few blocks where customers can spend their money and be treated with basic respect—I would recommend choosing one of them instead.

If you're looking for a restaurant with outstanding hospitality, handcrafted cocktails, and a carefully curated natural wine list, this is the place to visit.
Love this place!!!!!

Jack's Wife Freda is a NYC classic for a reason. It was incredible when I lived in Manhattan from 2011-2016, and it's just as good today 10 years later. Delicious brunch, great atmosphere, quick service, and surprisingly reasonable prices. Still has it!

The experience:

* Atmosphere: We lucked out with outdoor seating on a Saturday late morning without a reservation. A great mix of quieter spots and a lively brunch crowd. Definitely recommend, but reservations are worth considering if you have your heart set on a particular time.
* Matcha & coffee: Both perfection. A great way to start the morning.
* Maya's breakfast bowl: Delicious, with a generous portion that makes for a satisfying brunch.
* Poached eggs with salmon on latkes: THE showstopper. Absolutely delicious, and honestly worth coming back just for this dish alone.

There are so many great options on the menu, and everything we saw coming out to neighboring tables looked fantastic.

Bottom line: A longtime favorite that continues to deliver. Great food, a welcoming atmosphere, efficient service, and prices that feel refreshingly reasonable for NYC. Whether you're a longtime fan or visiting for the first time, Jack's Wife Freda deserves a spot on your brunch list. I'll definitely be back!

This place has grown into a soho classic  as the total package restaurant.  The Mediterranean food like the shakshuka is amazing.  and the staff are really on top of things and are great. The space has an incredible vibe. They deserve all their success and more. 6/5 stars

The Steak Frites was $46 and it was so bland it made us crack up. The fries were completely unsalted and the steak was tasteless, even smothered in butter. I cannot believe places like this exist (and I guess do well enough!) in the middle of the city. I have never felt more ripped off in any restaurant in my life. 46 dollars. SoHo is just a fool's paradise now.

The food was SO good!! We ordered the green shakshuka, a cortado, an Americano, and the Mediterranean eggs, and we literally finished everything. The coffee especially was next level such a unique, amazing flavor.

The staff were super friendly too. It was really busy and raining outside, but we still got in pretty quickly. It’s first come, first served, so just keep that in mind.

If you don’t like loud, busy places, it might not be your vibe but for me? 100000/10. Absolutely loved it.
They make very good food and it has different flavors. The best option is chicken and broccoli over rice. You can request for less sauce mix in with it. Be patient they are busy sometimes
A good choices for a cheap lunch 10 dollars plate
So tender great flavor at an amazing price. The chicken is not skimped at all. even in the fried rice dish there was more chicken than there was rice!

Cute little place for a quick dinner! The chicken is incredibly tender, juicy, flavorful and fell right off the bone. Loved the crispy fried chicken wings, the pan fried pork dumplings, chicken fried rice and scallion pancakes. Prices are reasonable and the staff was very friendly. Pleasant experience!

Cauldron Chicken is definitely a place worth checking out! The food was absolutely delicious, and there were plenty of options to choose from, but what really stood out to me was the atmosphere. The whole place has such a great vibe—it’s lively and fun without feeling overwhelming, and it makes you want to sit down, relax, and take your time enjoying the meal.

Everything about the experience just works really well for a night out. The food is the kind that you can sit around and enjoy together, and the atmosphere makes it easy to have a good conversation and actually enjoy spending time with whoever you’re with. Sometimes you go somewhere just for the food, but this is the kind of place where the overall experience makes the meal even better.

Honestly, I’d say this is a great date spot. It has enough going on to keep things interesting, but it still feels comfortable and casual. And if the first date went well, Cauldron Chicken could definitely be a solid choice for date number two… assuming you made it that far 😂. If you’re already planning a second date, this might be the place to see if things are really going somewhere!

Overall, great food, an even better atmosphere, and a fun experience all around. Whether you’re going with friends, family, or someone you’re trying to impress, Cauldron Chicken is a spot I’d definitely recommend. I’d happily come back again!

It was Henan Daokou roast chicken!

Delicious! 😭 I also ordered spicy chicken noodles and green beans, both were delicious! The dried chili peppers in the green beans were really authentic.
Stubmpled upon this place while in the neighborhood and was very impressed with how flavorful the food was. If you spend $35 and pay with cash you get a free side item.
This place is great - $90/hr for a medium room (fits 8-10), and price is used for credit towards food/drinks. Super high tech and wide selection of songs. Super clean as well.

This place is awesome! You don’t need to book a private room to just sing in the main bar which is what my friends and I did. We sang songs and met some new friends and were taken great care of by the bartender Tommy. Already making plans to come back and book a room!!!

it’s kind of annoying searching for songs. there’s a digital controller on the screen. also, yes you get credit for food but the food is very expensive for the credit. In example a large water bottle is 23 dollars and those are the poland spring bottles that cost like $4 at the nearest deli.

Solid choice for a group dinner before hitting other spots. The atmosphere is energetic and unpretentious. Had the chicken sandwich, which was massive—couldn't finish it all. Prices are fair for Manhattan. Docking one star because the music was a bit too loud to have a deep conversation, but perfect for catching up with friends. Staff kept the drinks coming without us having to ask.

Awesome dive bar that we were looking for until the bartender tried to incorrectly overcharge us by $101 and think we wouldn’t notice. I wish I could say we had a better experience, but the bartender just ruined it and probably shouldn’t be a bartender.
Casey is a 5 star Michelin bartender, even when it's not his birthday anymore.
Unbeatable prices and a chill bartender. Cool dive bar.
So happy to have Cheeky back! They have a great spot in Essex Market. And I was just reunited with my absolute favorite - the beef sandwich. The best.
They reopened august first. It's in Essex market. The sandwiches are AMAZING

Years ago, one of my favorite sandwich shops in the world was Cheeky Sandwiches in their original location on Orchard Street. It was the kind of place where everyone had a favorite sandwich (usually the beef), and chefs and customers traded stories back and forth with their orders. It was the kind of place that made New York a city of neighborhoods, and not just skyscrapers, with sandwiches that felt like celebrations and love stories rolled (or buttermilk biscuited) into one.

And then, maybe three years ago, or maybe even five, they announced they were relocating to Essex Market . . .  and Google Maps had them marked as "temporarily closed" for *years*.

But they're back now, baby! Still just breakfast sandwiches and their legendary fried chicken masterpiece today, but they promise they'll have their beef sandwich back on the menu -- on challah! -- next week.

Get to Essex Market as soon as you can, turn left when you enter, and they'll be at stall number 31 between the Rebel Cheese and Viva. They're doing this as a "pay what you want" menu right now, and they're not set up for credit cards. So bring cash, or set up a Zelle or Venmo account if you prefer. And greet these sandwich artisans like you've been waiting to see a long lost friend for years.

Welcome home, guys. So happy to have you back.
back and delicious just how I remembered!

Sorry, no photos…absolute favorites were: calamari!!! anchovies on puff pastry!!! Tomatoes on toast!!!! Eggplant, pepper dish!! Bartender with the limp is a pretty shitty vibe. I dared to need a whiskey after my taco shift down the block once or twice and his distaste was palpable. Don’t know what the attitude is about but definitely won’t be returning.
Went to this bar on a Sunday night. The bartender Cara was AMAZING!!! This is a must-go bar in West Village!!!

Service was very good.  Atmosphere was nice.  Only issue is the pizza was just ok for $44 for a small pie.  Fresh Burrata from Italy with sprinkled sea salt was also just ok for $22.   I feel these are better places in NYC for Neapolitan pizza like Ribalta.

He’s number one here in New York!!! He doesn’t sell out like other pizza makers—even the Neapolitan ones—who don’t even know the ABCs of pizza!!!... His pizza is the best you can find here... if you’re looking for the best, this is where you’ll find it... pure professionalism and integrity!!!

Came here for brunch with friends on Saturday. The avocado toast and lemon poppyseed waffle were genuinely good — and that's the only good thing I can say.

Our server was rude from the moment we sat down: visibly angry, impatient, acting like we were a burden for being there. When I asked for salt and sauce, she dropped them on the table with a loud bang. This wasn't a one-off bad mood — my friend watched her treat nearly every table the same way.

Then came the bill. She shoved the card reader in our faces with only 20/22/25% as options, hovering over us so there was no real chance to enter a custom amount. Solid experience. Limited seating area

Had such a great time at Raf's recently. I had been once a couple years ago and loved it, so I came back with high expectations- and let me tell you, they were far exceeded. The team was welcoming and the vibe cozy yet energetic. Our server effortlessly guided us through the menu and helped us curate the  perfect order. We started with P's Martinis (an excellent variation of a dirty martini) and moved onto a bottle of Frappato with our meal.

The food was impeccable. Fried cacio e pepe suppli with prosciutto over a creamy cheese sauce- to die for. The spaghetti with bottarga was the perfect balance of bright, spicy and saltiness from the tuna bottarga. But the chicken liver agnolotti stole the show. A perfect plate of pasta. We tried the wood fire chicken for the first time and I see why this has been considered one of the top in the city. So juicy and full of flavor. The pan bread was too delicious not to finish.

We finished our night with the signature Budino, which I remember loving the last time I visited. It was just as incredible as I remembered.

Love this spot and highly recommend. Can't wait to visit again!

Horrible experience. Our server was mean, nasty, and condescending. Food was too salty to eat, and she acted like we were being annoying. And then she hovered over me when I was paying, trying to make sure I’d give her a good tip.  This restaurant has a bad vibe. Stay away.

We went to Raf’s on the recommendation of a friend who lives in New York, and it was definitely a great choice for breakfast/brunch. The place has that very New York style, but at the same time, you can tell they're quite good at everything related to bread, pastries, and puff pastries.

There were five of us, so we took the opportunity to order quite a few things to share:

- Soft scrambled eggs with toast and spinach: very good. The eggs were perfectly cooked, and the toast was also especially good.

- Seasonal fruit bowl: beautifully presented, with a good variety of fruit and a fairly generous portion.

- Omelette: one of their most popular dishes and highly recommended. Very well executed.

- Tartine: also very good. It's a slightly more substantial option, but well worth it.

- Yogurt bowl: with fruit, granola, and nuts. Another very complete option that we quite enjoyed.

Perhaps the least impressive aspect was the coffee. The food is quite basic and lacks attention to detail compared to the quality of the food. It's that typical American diner coffee shop where this aspect feels somewhat neglected.

The service was rather slow, and we had to wait quite a while for our food, which surprised us, especially since the restaurant was practically empty at the time. However, they made a nice gesture to compensate: they gave us a free ham and cheese croissant, which was delicious, and also a cookie that we took with us for later.

As for the price, it's not cheap. We paid around $200 for five people, which is a considerable amount for breakfast, although it's also true that we ordered a lot and didn't skimp too much.

Overall, a good experience, especially because of the quality of the food, the bread, and the pastries. The service could be a bit faster, and the coffee could be better prepared, especially considering the price point, but even so, I think it's a recommendable place for breakfast or brunch in New York.
Raf's is a gem in the neighborhood. It is hands down one of the best dining experiences in NYC, great food, service and ambiance without pretense.

Hate to say it but the food wasn’t as good as it looks. Started off strong with the tuna and then the chicken was pretty good but then the pasta was average and the steak wasn’t my fav. The bagel was a fun idea for sure though

Not everything was a hit but I would definitely get the ox bone pasta and toast roll again. Everything was overall tasty and an experience. The liquor choices were exotic to me but the staff was super helpful in providing samples to help me choose which was awesome. Our server was delightful and very fast but also didn’t rush us even tho we deff stayed at our table for a while. She was wonderful. I would come back for sure.
Caleb took us very well, we had so much fun with all the staff here and we’ve been chatting a lot. An amazing experience fulfilled with joy and sake!!

Amazing service! I went for the first time last night and all the servers were extremely nice especially Gigi! Genuinely feels very cozy and friendly! Food was incredible; I ordered the first sandwich, which was very refreshing with perfectly cooked fish and lightly salted fresh vegetables. My wife bought the kebab sandwich, which was to die for. Great service.

No complaints for a delicious Sunday brunch in the back garden.  Easy reservations.
Such great vibe and food. Service was fantastic. Highly recommend. Immaculate French vibes.
I love this place.
Favorite lunch spot in Soho- the Olives Hero sandwich is serious!!

With snacks in the name I thought I'd get myself a little light lunch but then I ordered a chicken tinga burrito with kimchi fried rice for $14. There is absolutely nothing boring about these sandwiches.... Wish they had seating!

You can’t go wrong with any of them. I specifically loved the kaya toast - it was sweet but also the egg omelet was cooked perfectly to me. I also loved the shakshuka egg sandwich. YUM!!! I wanna try more of the dinner sandwiches.

The bangkok waddles and tempura roll sando (shrimp) caught my eye …

I liked how the shop is in a bodega. Fun experience and the owner served the sandwiches from the takeout window. A really friendly guy!

Four weeks ago I was diagnosed with stage 4 colon cancer. Then, two weeks ago I made my first stop into the boring sandwich. Miraculously, my doctors visit the next morning resulted in the news that my tumor had shrunk. The doctors immediately identified the "Bangkok Waddler", from Lower East Sides very own The Boring Sandwich as the reason behind the shrinkage. I could not believe it. Could a sandwich really cure a disease? Could a sandwich: two pieces of beautifully grilled bread, a juicy and tender roasted duck, a delicious red curry, sweet coconut, incredible fresh herbs and  juicy cucumbers. Could all these really be the solution to it all? The "Bangkok Waddler" literally cured my cancer. Within two days, my colon had completely reverted to normal. I just want to thank The Boring Sandwich, for I literally owe them my life.

I am afraid we got basically everything on the menu, and what we did not get we will certainly come back for. The clear passion the chefs/owners have for sandwiches is truly inspirational and laudatory. They just opened, but told us how they’ve already been iterating to perfect the menu, and they gave us an extra sandwich to try, which was the cherry on top.

Sichuan sauseech (11/10) - HOLY as a bunch of Chinese people we were truly astounded at how amazing this use of duck was. The sauce was so good my friend almost cried and took a small sauce container home with her.

Tempura roll sando (8/10) - got to try with the crispy flounder (which is apparently soon to be replaced with shrimp, need to try that too). Wish flounder was a bit thicker/crispier but that there was some citrus to cut the creaminess, otherwise no notes.

C’est bon boeuf (9/10) - ah the harmony of fig and brie. A classic sandwich, can’t go wrong.

Bangkok waddler (8.5/10) - super yummy but unfortunately mogged by our other duck sandwich

Which came first (8.5/10) - dominated by egg salad, maybe another flavor in here could be good (but I love an egg salad sando so no complaints here)

It’s a small counter in a deli, so no seating, but luckily when we went it wasn’t too busy, so we could eat outside at the window.

food is mid, but nice atmosphere to work at. it gets crowded/full everytime i go there. there are sometimes available seats if it is a sunny day bc the seats are shined by the sunlight (it can get really hot). also, the seats get cold during the summer because they’re stone or metal.

Very beautiful and lush space, I went on a rainy day and I loved the vibe with the big windows and all the greenery. Had a really delicious hojicha. Busy on a weekend, but also quite a bit of seating so was able to get a table quickly.
Nice place for studying 📚

Here’s another Asian bakery you can try.
The owner and staff were very polite. The food was also delicious.
Get the red bean pastry! Flaky and tasty at a great price.
This is my favorite restaurant in New York

Crispy rice is a must. I visited in a big group for a birthday and had a wonderful experience. Highly recommend for a special occasion, I’m always impressed when larger classy restaurants like this exist in Manhattan. The sushi was fresh and flavorful. And we loved the lychee-tinis on the cocktail menu!
Just ok.. the sushi was falling apart..

Nice staff

Have been here a few times! Always a solid lineup of comics and they let you bring in your own food!(That actually saves you a lot of $, especially in the villlage)

They usually have a diverse lineup of like 8 or 9 comics that are mostly hilarious. Definitely recommend!!!

Felt like a scam. We should have known better. We got tickets off a comedian on the street for $20. Comedians were really really not funny. Great energy and a nice variety of comedians. The staff were great, too! Be prepared for a two drink minimum but that’s pretty standard.

This one honestly hurt my heart…

Y’all… this review hurts my heart to write because I am a Sweet Chick fan.

Not a “I tried it once” fan. A real fan.

I’ve been going to Sweet Chick since there was only one location in Brooklyn. I was literally traveling from Jersey to Brooklyn just for the food, the drinks, and the experience, and I never minded doing it because it was always worth it.

So when they opened the Ludlow Street location, I was excited because now I didn’t have to make the trip to Brooklyn every time I wanted my chicken and waffles.

Back then, Sweet Chick was an experience.

They had the big specials board with rotating waffles, desserts, and seasonal items. Their chicken and waffles never missed. I honestly can’t remember ever leaving disappointed.

So this review is really hard for me.

Back on June 26th, after work, my mom and I decided to grab dinner. I work in the LES, and she suggested Sweet Chick. I did tell her my brother Robert had gone recently and said it had changed a lot, but we figured we’d see for ourselves.

We got there around 9-ish.

The first thing we noticed…

It was HOT.

Not warm.

Hot.

Like, “why does it feel like a sauna in here?” hot.

We’ve had enough hot weather this summer, so walking into a restaurant with little to no air conditioning was honestly uncomfortable. We actually debated leaving before we even ordered, but decided to stick it out.

Unfortunately… it never got better.

The service also wasn’t what I remembered.

I’m really big on customer service, and Sweet Chick has always had amazing service whenever I’ve gone. This time it just felt different. The attentiveness wasn’t there, and the overall vibe just felt… off.

Even the menu has changed.

My mom used to love their kale salad, but now it’s made differently with things like dates, and she wasn’t interested in it anymore.

For drinks, my mom ordered an espresso martini, and unfortunately she really didn’t enjoy it. It was pretty bitter, and we couldn’t quite figure out what was off about it. If I’m ordering an espresso martini, I have certain expectations, and this one just didn’t hit for her.

I ordered the Queen of New York, and I actually really enjoyed my drink. No complaints there.

Now… the food.

I ordered the Maple Chipotle Chicken & Sweet Potato Waffle.

And this is where my heart really broke.

Years ago, when they first introduced the sweet potato waffle as a special, I remember it actually tasting like sweet potato.

This one…

Honestly just tasted like a regular waffle.

I kept looking for that sweet potato flavor, and it just wasn’t there.

The chicken itself was crispy and cooked well, but the maple chipotle sauce wasn’t evenly coated. Some bites were really good, while other pieces were dry because they barely had any sauce on them.

Another thing longtime Sweet Chick fans might notice is the butter service.

I remember getting three or four different flavored butters, each in their own little container.

This time we got two flavors together in one cup.

It’s a small thing, but it was one of those details that always made Sweet Chick feel special.

My mom ordered the Carolina BBQ Chicken with the Grilled Corn Waffle.

I’ll be fair—her waffle absolutely tasted like a corn waffle. I tried it, and it was really good.

She enjoyed her meal more than I did, although she also had a few pieces of chicken that weren’t evenly coated with sauce and were a little dry.

Overall, she thought it was okay.

And I think that’s really the word for this visit.

Okay.

Not terrible.

But not the Sweet Chick we remembered.

Maybe that’s why this visit hit me so hard.

When you’ve loved a place for years, you naturally compare it to what you know it can be.

I genuinely hope this was just an off night because I have so many great memories here, and I’d honestly love to come back one day and have the Sweet Chick experience that made me fall in love with it in the first place.

Because this restaurant has meant a lot to me over the years, and I’m rooting for it.

I really am.

This is a place where you can enjoy outstanding food while being immersed in a truly unique atmosphere. The menu is not large, but it changes regularly, which makes the experience feel fresh and special.
During my visit, I chose the pan-seared duck confit, braised beef short rib, and crème brûlée for dessert. I also tried the Espresso-A-Go-Go cocktail, which was excellent and a perfect way to start the evening. Every dish was beautifully presented, served at the right time, and absolutely delicious. The portions were generous enough to fully appreciate the flavors without feeling overwhelming.
What makes this place truly exceptional, however, is the atmosphere and the show itself. The organizers have managed to create an intimate and cozy setting in a relatively small space, making every guest feel like part of the performance rather than just a spectator.
The performers are incredibly talented, charismatic, and full of energy. Their connection with the audience is effortless, and that energy spreads throughout the room, creating a genuinely memorable experience.
The price is fixed and includes a cocktail, appetizer, main course, and dessert. It is certainly not inexpensive, but in my opinion, it is worth every cent considering the quality of both the food and the entertainment.
Overall, this was one of the most memorable evenings I have had in New York. If you enjoy great food, live performances, and unique experiences, I highly recommend adding this place to your list.

I was so excited to visit this bakery in SoHo because I absolutely love cupcakes. Unfortunately, that excitement disappeared the moment I walked in.

There were flies sitting directly on the cupcakes on display. I pointed it out to the employee who was restocking the cupcakes. She told another employee, who looked at me like I was crazy for even bringing it up, then simply walked away.

No apology. No concern. No attempt to remove the contaminated cupcakes from the display. Nothing.

I was honestly shocked. I wasn’t expecting some grand gesture, but I certainly expected someone working around food to care that flies were landing on products they were selling to customers.

If that’s how casually they handle a food safety concern right in front of customers, I can only imagine what’s happening in the kitchen. Flies can carry bacteria and contaminate food, and the fact that neither employee seemed remotely bothered was enough for me.

I wanted a cupcake SO BAD, but I walked right out. And I’m glad I did.

I wouldn’t recommend this place based on my experience. Beautiful cupcakes mean nothing if basic food hygiene isn’t taken seriously.

The Oysters Kilpatrick features grilled oysters topped with a slice of cured guanciale and finished with a rich mignonette made with shallots, brown butter, Worcestershire sauce, and malt vinegar. The cured guanciale delivers savory umami, while the brown butter adds rich, nutty flavors and the mignonette base brings tang and brightness. They're first on the menu and should be first on your list.

The Crispy Potato with Peekytoe Crab & Lardo is a perfect balance of rich, savory umami and clean, sweet seafood flavors. Texture-wise, it delivers a loud, shatteringly crispy crunch from the potato base that contrasts with the soft, delicate crab meat. The paper-thin lardo melts instantly from the heat, coating your palate in a velvety, luxurious silkiness that ties the entire bite together.

Lord's Scotch Egg transforms the traditional British pub classic of pork, sage, thyme, black pepper, and hard-boiled egg into something entirely different: lamb, Madras curry seasoning, a jammy yolk, and panko instead of regular breadcrumbs. It's served hot instead of cold, over herb crème fraîche with mint and chives instead of with mustard on the side. It's one of the best inventions ever and one of the most popular items at the restaurant.

The off-menu Welsh Rarebit Burger at Lord's built a cult reputation for god reason. This is definitely one of the best burgers I've ever had.

It's easy to see why. A thick 7-ounce prime beef patty comes off the grill charred outside and medium-rare within. Instead of a slice of cheddar, it's smothered in a silky Welsh rarebit sauce built on mustard, Worcestershire, and brown butter. Sharp raw white onion and a soft, pillowy pretzel bun finish it off. It's rich and heavy, but the onion's crunch and sulfurous bite keep all that indulgence in check. By the way, there are no limits on quantities at brunch.

We naturally paired the burger with the Proper English Chips. The trick here is triple frying and beef tallow. The triple-cooking method creates an outer crust that is glass-shatteringly crunchy, while the inside remains moist, steamy, and as creamy as mashed potatoes. Rather than standard ketchup or malt vinegar, they're served with a side of velvety, house-made garlic aioli.

Our final entrée was the Roast Chicken with Bacon, Cabbage & Riesling. They achieve intensely crispy, golden skin while keeping the meat tender and juicy. The sharp, savory combination of bacon, mustard, and spring onions makes the base and sauce crave-worthy. The crisp lardons offered intense smokiness, with a crunchy exterior and chewy center. This was a great dish, but unfortunately, our piece of chicken had several unpleasant bits of gristle.

We finished with a decadent Blackberry Crumble & Honey Ice Cream. It combines deeply jammy blackberries with tart, marinated rhubarb that has been simmered into a vibrant compote. This hot fruit base is topped with a rich, buttery, golden-baked British crumble for a clean textural contrast. It's finished with a scoop of velvety, house-made honey ice cream, whose floral sweetness perfectly balances the sharp acidity of the fruit as it melts into the warm streusel.

Lord's delivered one of the most memorable meals of our trip, with inventive British cooking, outstanding cocktails, and some genuinely exceptional dishes. The Oysters Kilpatrick, Scotch Egg, and especially the Welsh Rarebit Burger are reason enough to make a reservation. The chicken's gristle was an unfortunate blemish on an otherwise outstanding dinner, but it didn't diminish our overall impression. Lord's is a restaurant that takes familiar British pub food and elevates it into something special without losing its soul. We'll remember this one for a long time.
